# NudoIQ

> NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for carriers who haul on Amazon Relay: owner-operators, small fleets and dispatchers. It runs inside the Amazon Relay load board in the carrier's own signed-in browser tab and adds load board refreshing, rule-based alerts and booking, lane rate history, net profit per load and scorecard dispute letter drafting. It costs $49.99 a month for every feature, with a 7-day free trial and no card needed to start. NudoIQ is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by Amazon. It is published by Sami Enterprises LLC, Portland, Oregon.

## What it does

- **Refresher:** reloads the Amazon Relay load board at an interval the carrier sets.
- **Control bar with three modes:** Alert (pings you when a load matches your rules), Search (refreshes quietly and floats new and price-up loads that clear your minimums to the top) and Autobook (books a matching load for you). Rules: Min Net Profit, Min $/Mile, a load-pay minimum and a max-books cap per START; lanes come from Relay search. Autobook stops at the cap and the profit floor.
- **Telegram alerts** when a load lands, if you connect Telegram.
- **Instant Book:** books a load in one action from the control bar instead of the multi-step flow.
- **Lane Intelligence:** compares the posted price with 90 days of that lane's history and shows a target rate, an expected range and a confidence level. Decision support, not a guarantee.
- **Net Profit on every load card:** posted rate minus driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead to pickup, in dollars and net rate per mile. Loads below a set profit floor can be hidden.
- **Scorecard dispute letters:** reads the carrier's Relay scorecard, identifies the violation behind the score and drafts a dispute letter citing Amazon policy. The carrier reviews, edits and submits it.
- **Backhaul finder:** searches loads from where the current load ends, pointed back toward home within a set radius and day window. Sorts by total pay, rate per mile, pickup time or distance home; the all-in rate counts the deadhead.
- **Post A Truck helper:** shows origin, destination, distance and board price next to the carrier's minimum rate per mile and minimum payout, then posts with one button.
- **Route check:** opens the routed trip, with every stop, in Google Maps (standard routing, not truck-specific).
- English and Spanish interface.

## Pricing

- $49.99 per month, every feature included, the same price for one truck or twenty.
- 7-day free trial for first-time signups, no card needed to start.
- Cancel anytime from the Stripe customer portal. Payments are processed by Stripe.
- Rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store. Used by 300+ carriers.

## Requirements

- Desktop Google Chrome.
- An approved Amazon Relay carrier account. NudoIQ works inside the carrier's own signed-in Relay session; it does not create or grant Relay access.

## Important limitations

- NudoIQ does not guarantee loads, bookings, rates or earnings. Pay on Amazon Relay varies by lane, timing and equipment.
- Lane rate estimates are decision support based on past lane data, not a promise of what a load will pay.
- Dispute letters are drafts. Amazon decides every scorecard dispute, and NudoIQ cannot influence or promise the outcome.
- NudoIQ is not made by Amazon and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by Amazon.

- The only Amazon Relay extension that books loads to the carrier's own minimum net profit after driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead (checked October 5, 2026, across 52 other Relay listings on the Chrome Web Store).
- The only Amazon Relay extension that drafts scorecard dispute letters; the carrier submits and Amazon decides (checked October 5, 2026).
- One flat price: $49.99 a month for every feature, the same for one truck or twenty; 7-day free trial, no card needed to start.

- Rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store and used by 300+ carriers.
- Side-by-side with six other Relay extensions: https://nudoiq.com/why-nudoiq/

NudoIQ analyzed public FMCSA roadside inspection records that list Amazon as the shipper. From 2023-09-24 to 2026-09-22, 101,444 inspections listed Amazon as the shipper, across 22,866 distinct carriers (USDOT numbers); about 530 carriers per month appear for the first time, and about 70% of carriers with an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025 run 1-5 power units. Counts are a floor (most loads are never inspected) and cover Amazon freight in general, not only Amazon Relay loads. Full method, charts and caveats: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/

NudoIQ also publishes Amazon Relay lane rates from loads its users saw on the Amazon Relay board: 4,066 distinct loads first seen July 7 to October 5, 2026, mostly starting in Tennessee. One-way loads had a median final board price of $2.90 per mile and round trips $2.36 per mile; 57% of loads were raised in price while posted. These are observed board prices, not carrier earnings, and Amazon did not provide the data. Lanes, method and caveats: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-rates/

# How the Amazon Relay Load Board Works

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: The Amazon Relay load board, at relay.amazon.com, is where approved carriers find and book Amazon freight. It's open 24/7 and free to search and book, with filters for equipment, load type, radius, trip length and time windows.

## What the Load Board Is

The Amazon Relay load board is your direct connection to loads that Amazon Logistics needs moved. You log in at relay.amazon.com with your carrier credentials, see available loads, and book them. It's the only place Amazon posts loads for Relay carriers. Third-party load boards and brokers don't carry Amazon's freight.

When you sign in, you see a list of loads posted that day. Each load card shows the pickup location, delivery location, the load type, the posted rate, and other details you need to decide whether to book it.

## Why Loads Vanish So Quickly

Good loads disappear within seconds of posting because the board attracts many active carriers watching for work. The moment a profitable load lands, multiple carriers see it at once and one of them books it first. This is why many carriers refresh the load board constantly: they're trying to catch good loads before anyone else does.

A manual refresh means you walk away, come back, hit reload, and check what's new. But if you step away for five minutes, you miss dozens of refreshes and all the loads that posted in that window. That's why carriers use [refreshers](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) and [auto-booker extensions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) to stay in the competition.

## Reading a Load Card

Every load card on the board shows the same core information, though the layout varies depending on your device and which extension you're using.

**Origin and Destination**: The pickup location and drop-off location. These are what drive the rate and determine whether the load fits your dispatch plan.

**Equipment Type**: What the load is (box truck, dry van, reefer, container). Amazon accepts day cab and sleeper tractors, 26 ft and 16 ft [box trucks with tuck-under liftgates](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck/), 48 ft and 53 ft dry van and reefer trailers, and 20/40/45 ft high-cube containers. Cargo vans are not supported.

**Posted Rate**: The dollar amount Amazon is paying for that load. This is the gross rate, before driver pay, fuel, maintenance, and deadhead. Many carriers now use [Net Profit tools](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) to see what you actually keep after costs.

**Load Type**: One-way or round-trip. One-way loads move freight in one direction. Round-trip loads start and end at the same domicile. You can also get loads through Post A Truck, where you post your availability and get matched.

## Filters and Search

The built-in filters narrow down what you see. You can filter by origin and destination (or radius), equipment type, trailer status, load type, driver type, max stops, trip length, rate range, and pickup and delivery windows, and save the searches you use most. Filters save time because you don't have to look at every load posted.

If you're only moving dry vans, filtering out box truck loads means less scrolling. If you have a home hub and want work headed toward it, filtering by destination narrows the list. The more specific your filter, the faster you can scan for loads that match your operation.

## How Rates Are Set

Amazon sets the rate for each load based on several factors: the season, the time of day, the origin, the equipment type, your booking history, and the day's load volume. The same lane posted at 6 a.m. might pay differently at noon because the volume and demand shifted.

This means two identical lanes can pay completely different amounts depending on when they post. Understanding that rates move with demand, and not taking it personally when a rate looks low, is part of the business.

## Refreshing and Staying Competitive

Manual refreshing works if you're sitting at your computer all day, but most owner-operators can't camp on the load board. Refreshing every 30 seconds by hand isn't practical. A [refresh extension](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) solves this by automating the reload on an interval you set.


Once you have a refresher running, you can set an alert to ping you when a load matching your rules posts, or use a search highlight to spot matching loads visually, or set up an auto-booker to book them for you automatically if you've set a profit floor and max-books cap.

## Load Types and Booking Methods

**Spot Loads**: One-way and round-trip loads you find and book yourself. Book, complete before 11:59 pm Saturday, and get paid Friday.

**Blocks**: A chunk of time you reserve trucks and drivers for Relay. Amazon pays for the block even if it doesn't use all of it.

**Short-Term Contracts**: Full or partial weeks of loads booked in advance. New contracts need a B grade or better.

**Post A Truck**: You post your truck's availability and a minimum rate per mile, and Amazon matches you with loads. Matched carriers see that freight before it reaches the board.

Each method works differently. Spot loads are quickest and give you the most control. Blocks commit your truck and driver for a set time. Contracts provide stability. Post A Truck lets you set your own minimum rate and wait for matches.

## The Scorecard and Load Access

Amazon grades your performance on four metrics: on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free (stationary trailers and loads with no assigned driver). Your overall score is the lowest of the four, and low grades can limit your access to loads. Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explains each metric.

If you accept a load and then cancel it, that counts against you, and the closer to pickup, the bigger the penalty. If you miss a pickup window, that counts. If you believe a score impact is wrong, you can dispute it in your Relay account (Amazon decides the outcome), or work on the metrics to rebuild your score.

## Where NudoIQ Fits

NudoIQ runs inside the Relay load board in your browser. It adds a control bar with three modes: Alert (pings you on a match), Search (refreshes quietly and floats new and price-up loads that clear your minimums to the top) and Autobook (books automatically). You set up rules once and stop watching manually.

It also shows [Lane Intelligence](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) next to each rate, so you can see what that lane normally pays and whether today's rate is high or low. A [Net Profit calculator](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) shows you the dollars left after driver pay, fuel, maintenance, and deadhead to pickup, so you can set a profit floor and only book loads that clear it.

You can also use it to find backhaul loads from where your current load ends, headed back toward home, and to draft dispute letters when your scorecard gets dinged. It's a refresher, booker, rate calculator, and dispute tool all in one extension.

Choosing an extension for your board? Here's [LoadFetcher and NudoIQ, compared point by point](https://nudoiq.com/loadfetcher-alternative/).

## Getting Started

To use the load board, you need a carrier account with Amazon Relay. That requires a DOT number with interstate authority, active for at least 180 days; a valid MC number; an FMCSA safety rating of Satisfactory, None or Not Rated; BASIC scores under Amazon's limits; insurance minimums (GL $1M per occurrence, auto liability $1M, cargo at least $100K); and the right equipment.

Once you're approved, log in at relay.amazon.com, sign in with your carrier credentials, and you'll see the load board. From there, the board is yours to use as-is, or you can add a [refresher extension](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) or [booking tool](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) to work smarter.

## Better Load Board Decisions with NudoIQ

Managing the Relay load board by hand (refreshing, reading rates, judging whether a load is worth it, and handling disputes) takes time and focus. NudoIQ automates the refresh, surfaces rate history, calculates profit, and drafts dispute letters for you.

The extension runs inside the board tab in your signed-in browser and works on desktop Chrome with an English or Spanish interface. It costs $49.99 a month for every feature, with a 7-day free trial and no card needed to start. Cancel anytime from your Stripe portal.

Used by 300+ carriers and rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store, NudoIQ is built to work the way you work. Start free for seven days, see what it does, and cancel if it's not for you.

## Frequently asked questions

### What time do Amazon Relay loads post on the load board?
Loads post throughout the day as Amazon needs freight moved. There's no set time, and Amazon says volume nearly doubles during peak seasons like Prime Day and the holidays. This is why refreshing helps you catch them.

### Can I book Amazon loads from a third-party load board?
No. Amazon only posts loads on the Relay load board. Brokers and third-party platforms don't carry Amazon freight. You must use relay.amazon.com to find and book Amazon work.

### Why do good Amazon Relay loads get booked so fast?
Many Relay carriers watch the same load board. When a profitable load posts, multiple carriers see it in the same second. The fastest person to click gets it. This is why carriers use refresher extensions: to reload the board automatically instead of by hand, so they see good loads sooner.

### How do I know if an Amazon Relay rate is good?
Rates vary by lane, time of day, season, and volume. The same route can pay very differently hour to hour. The best way to judge a rate is to track what that lane has paid over the past 90 days, calculate your net profit after all costs (driver pay, fuel, maintenance, deadhead), and set a profit floor: don't book loads that don't clear it. [Lane Intelligence tools](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) show you the history; a [profit calculator](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) shows you the net dollars.

### What loads can I book with different equipment?
Box truck loads are for 26 ft and 16 ft trucks with tuck-under liftgates. Tractor loads are for day cab and sleeper units moving 48/53 ft trailers or containers. The board filters by equipment type. Check which equipment you're registered with Relay and filter to loads that match it.

### How often should I refresh the load board?
[Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) the board auto-refreshes new spot freight matches every 30 seconds. A [refresh extension](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) reloads more often, on an interval you set. This keeps you in the hunt for loads without you staring at the screen. Set the refresh interval based on your tolerance for alert noise and your internet connection.

### Is there an Amazon Relay load board for cargo vans?
No. Amazon says cargo vans cannot be used for loads on Amazon Relay, so there are no van loads on the board. The smallest supported truck is a 16 ft dock-height box truck with a working tuck-under liftgate. Our guide to [using a cargo van for Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cargo-van/) covers what to run instead.

### How do I find power only loads on the Amazon Relay load board?
Use the equipment type and trailer status filters so you only see loads your tractor can pull. Amazon says most Relay loads are power only: you bring the tractor and Relay supplies the trailer. If you want weeks of work booked ahead instead of one load at a time, read how [Amazon Relay contracts](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contracts/) work; new contracts need a B grade or better.

# What Is Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/what-is-amazon-relay/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Amazon Relay is Amazon's platform for carriers to find and book Amazon freight. Approved carriers book spot loads, blocks and short-term contracts, or post availability with Post A Truck. Amazon pays weekly and grades carriers on a performance score.

## Overview

Amazon Relay is an on-demand load board built directly into Amazon's fulfillment network. Unlike traditional freight boards where shippers post lanes and carriers bid, Amazon Relay is where Amazon posts its own work: one-way loads, round trips, blocks and short-term contracts. Loads are booked first-come, first-served through the load board, meaning that fast refreshing and split-second booking decisions determine who gets the best freight.

Amazon says there's no fleet size requirement, so owner-operators and small fleets can use it. You sign in with an Amazon account, and Amazon tenders its loads only through Relay. Spot loads show an all-in price you can book as listed. You can also post your truck with the **Post A Truck** feature, set a minimum rate per mile, and get matched to work.

If you have a car rather than a truck, see [Amazon Relay vs Amazon Flex](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-vs-amazon-flex/).

## Who Can Join Amazon Relay

Amazon has specific eligibility requirements to protect load security and ensure compliance:

- Your DOT number must have interstate authority, and Relay typically requires it to be at least 180 days old to complete onboarding. If yours is newer, Amazon's Relay FAQ still encourages you to apply early.
- You must have a valid MC (Motor Carrier) number.
- Your FMCSA safety rating must be Satisfactory, None, or Not Rated. A rating below Satisfactory disqualifies you.
- Your BASIC scores must stay within limits: Unsafe Driving below 60%, HOS Compliance below 60%, Vehicle Maintenance below 75%, Controlled Substances/Alcohol below 75%, Driver Fitness below 75%. Your driver out-of-service violation rate must be at or below 35%, and vehicle violation rate at or below 50%.
- Amazon verifies your business entity and every beneficial owner, meaning anyone with more than 25% ownership in your carrier.

The 180-day authority rule is the main gate for new carriers. Amazon's FAQ says rejected applicants may be able to reapply once a fixable issue (such as authority status) is resolved.

Ready to apply? Our guide to [how to sign up for Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/how-to-sign-up-for-amazon-relay/) walks through Amazon's five application steps.

## What Equipment Works on Relay

Relay supports specific equipment types, and what you own affects your load volume and rates:

- Day cab and sleeper tractors (most loads available)
- 26 ft and 16 ft box trucks with a working tuck-under liftgate (the liftgate is required)
- 48 ft and 53 ft dry van and reefer trailers
- 20, 40 and 45 ft high-cube containers (UIIA compliant)

**Cargo vans are not supported: this is an explicit exclusion.** Even if you think a large cargo van could handle loads, Amazon does not accept it on the platform.

Amazon says the majority of Relay loads are [power only](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/): you bring the tractor and Amazon provides the trailer. A [2024 Amazon post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-work-amazon-relay) says round trips usually need only a tractor, and that for one-way loads you'll "most likely" need a box truck or your own trailer.

## How Loads Get Posted and Booked

Amazon tenders loads only through the Relay [load board](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/): not on third-party boards, DATs, or by email. When you log in to Relay, you see every available load that matches your equipment type in real time.

There are four main ways to find work on Relay:

### The Load Board
Browse one-way and round-trip loads instantly. You see the posted rate, origin, destination, and estimated pick-up time before you commit. Book immediately if it fits your route and profit requirements. Good loads book within seconds, which is why [auto-refresh tools](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) and browser extensions exist.

### Blocks
A chunk of time you reserve trucks and drivers for Relay. Amazon pays for the block even if it doesn't use the full block.

### Short-Term Contracts
Short-term contracts cover full or partial weeks of loads, booked in advance. New contracts need a B grade or better, and freight auctions let carriers bid on contracts of up to 6 months.

### Post A Truck
Instead of hunting the board, you post your truck's availability up to two weeks ahead with a minimum rate per mile, and Amazon matches you to loads. This reduces the need for constant refreshing and is helpful for carriers who want steadier work.

## Understanding the Performance Scorecard

Amazon grades carriers on four metrics, based on the last six weeks of hauls:

- **On-time**: Loads arriving by the planned time at origin and destination.
- **Acceptance**: How often you cancel loads you booked, including expired loads. The closer to pickup, the bigger the penalty.
- **App usage**: Drivers keeping the Relay app running with location on for the whole trip.
- **Disruption-free**: No stationary trailers and no loads without an assigned driver.

Your overall score is the lowest of the four, shown as a letter grade from F to A+. The grade affects which work you can book, such as new contracts and early access to new spot loads. If something happens in transit, you can dispute a score impact in your Relay account, and Amazon makes the final decision. See our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) for details.

## Pay Cycle and Rate Variability

Amazon pays weekly. Your pay cycle runs Sunday to Saturday. Any load you complete before 11:59 pm Saturday gets paid the following Friday. Invoices are generated automatically, so there's no invoice chase needed.

Load rates on Amazon Relay vary based on multiple factors: season, time of day, pickup origin, delivery destination, your equipment type, your own booking history and how many other carriers are online that day. The same lane can pay very differently on different days, depending on Amazon's demand and your carrier profile. This is why learning to read a [lane's rate history](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) is important: it gives you context for whether a posted rate is good or soft.

## Where NudoIQ Fits In

Many carriers use [Amazon Relay auto-refresh](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) tools or [auto-booking extensions](https://nudoiq.com/best-amazon-relay-extensions/) to speed up their workflow. If you want to automate refreshing, understand [lane rate history](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) to judge a price, or draft dispute letters based on [scorecard violations](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/), NudoIQ adds intelligence on top of the Relay board itself. It keeps the board fresh with configurable intervals, books loads by your rules (price floor, lane preferences, max-book cap), shows you net profit per load after fuel and deadhead costs, and drafts dispute letters based on Amazon's policy.

NudoIQ costs **$49.99 per month** for every feature: the same price whether you run one truck or twenty. Start with a **7-day free trial**, no card needed to start. Cancel anytime from the Stripe portal. **5.0 rating** on the Chrome Web Store. Used by 300+ carriers.

Our [Amazon Relay Chrome extension guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-chrome-extension/) shows what NudoIQ adds to your Relay tab and how to set it up.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I sign in to Amazon Relay?
Visit relay.amazon.com and sign in with your existing Amazon shopping account, or create a new one. You'll complete Amazon's approval process, which includes verifying your DOT number, MC number, insurance, safety rating and beneficial ownership. Amazon's Relay FAQ says a completed application is typically approved or rejected within 1 to 3 weeks.

### Can I run Amazon Relay part-time?
Yes. You set your own availability with Post A Truck, and you choose which loads to book on the board. Amazon says there's no fleet size requirement. Just remember that cancelling loads you booked hurts your acceptance score.

### What happens if I miss a pickup?
A late or missed pickup counts against your on-time metric, which Amazon measures from your check-in time at the site, and a lower grade can reduce your load access. If something happens along the way, Amazon says you can let Relay know and dispute the score impact. Our free [dispute letter tool](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-dispute-letter/) helps you write it up.

### Does my scorecard affect how much I get paid?
Amazon doesn't say your grade changes a load's price. It changes access: A+, A and B+ carriers see new spot loads first, B and above can book new contracts, and higher grades get priority matching on Post A Truck.

### Is there a minimum rate or maximum distance?
Amazon doesn't publish a minimum rate. You decide whether a posted rate justifies your cost to run it, and with Post A Truck you can set your own minimum rate per mile. Many carriers set their own profit floor and reject anything below: NudoIQ lets you set that rule and filter loads automatically.

### Can I use a cargo van?
No. Amazon Relay does not accept cargo vans. Only box trucks 16 ft and 26 ft with a working tuck-under liftgate, tractors with trailers, or supported containers.

# Amazon Relay Requirements

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Amazon Relay requires a DOT number with interstate authority active for at least 180 days, a valid MC number, and an FMCSA safety rating of Satisfactory, None or Not Rated. Insurance must meet its minimums and equipment must be supported.

## Authority and Operational Requirements

Before you can book your first load on Amazon Relay, your business must meet these foundational criteria:

**DOT Number**
You need a DOT number with interstate authority, and Relay typically requires that authority to be at least 180 days old to complete onboarding. If yours is newer, you can still apply. Amazon's Relay FAQ says "we encourage you to apply early," so it can start reviewing your information.

**MC (Motor Carrier) Number**
You must have a valid MC number. This number, issued by the FMCSA, shows that you're registered as an interstate carrier. When you get your DOT number, the MC application is usually filed at the same time.

**Authority Age**
Relay typically requires your DOT number to be at least 180 days old to complete onboarding, and Amazon encourages you to apply early. Amazon words the rule four ways; our [new authority guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-new-authority/) puts them side by side.

## Safety Rating and BASIC Score Requirements

Amazon requires a satisfactory safety profile. Amazon will check your FMCSA records, including your safety rating and your BASIC (Behavior Analysis and Safety Improvement Categories) scores.

**FMCSA Safety Rating**
Your safety rating must be one of these three: Satisfactory, None, or Not Rated. Any rating below Satisfactory (such as Conditional or Unsatisfactory) disqualifies you from Relay.

**BASIC Score Limits**
Your BASIC scores must stay within these limits:
- Unsafe Driving: below 60%
- HOS Compliance: below 60%
- Vehicle Maintenance: below 75%
- Controlled Substances/Alcohol: below 75%
- Driver Fitness: below 75%

Additionally, your driver out-of-service violation rate must be at or below 35%, and your vehicle violation rate must be at or below 50%.

These thresholds reflect Amazon's risk tolerance. If you're close to any limit, focus on improving that metric before applying. A violation that pushes you over the limit can delay approval.

## Insurance Minimums

[Insurance requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/) are strict and non-negotiable. Here's a summary; see the full insurance page for details on each coverage:

- **Commercial General Liability**: $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate
- **Auto Liability**: $1,000,000 per occurrence, including $50,000 trailer replacement (trailer interchange) coverage
- **Cargo Insurance**: at least $100,000
- **Workers' Compensation**: the FAQ says "in all jurisdictions where your company operates"; $100,000 per occurrence for Employer's Liability. See our [workers' comp guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-workers-comp/)

You'll need to upload proof of insurance to your Relay account. Amazon verifies these minimums before approving you.

## Equipment Specifications

Amazon accepts only specific types of equipment. Your [equipment choices](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck/) determine what loads you can book:

- Day cab tractors (single-engine cab, no sleeper)
- Sleeper tractors (with sleeping compartment)
- 26 ft and 16 ft box trucks with a working tuck-under liftgate (the liftgate is required)
- 48 ft and 53 ft dry van trailers
- 53 ft reefer trailers (temperature-controlled)
- 20, 40 and 45 ft high-cube containers (UIIA compliant)

**Cargo vans are not supported.** Do not apply with a cargo van: Amazon will not approve it, even if you think it meets the load specs.

Amazon says the majority of Relay loads are power only (you bring the tractor, Amazon provides the trailer), and one-way loads will most likely need a box truck or your own trailer.

Running a box truck without a CDL? See [Amazon Relay non-CDL](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-non-cdl/).

## Beneficial Owner Verification

Amazon verifies the ownership of your carrier. This means:

- Amazon verifies your business entity (LLC, S-Corp, Sole Proprietorship, etc.).
- Amazon verifies every beneficial owner, anyone with more than 25% ownership, using government records and documentation you provide.

During the sign-up process, you'll be asked to provide ownership information. Have your business formation documents, tax ID and ownership structure ready.

If owners are changing because of a sale, see [Amazon Relay business for sale](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-business-for-sale/).

## Steps to Sign Up for Amazon Relay

Amazon's application has five steps, in this order: DOT number, company details, one-time password verification, equipment inventory and payment information. You sign in with an existing Amazon shopping account or create a new one, and your details should match your FMCSA record. Our guide to [how to sign up for Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/how-to-sign-up-for-amazon-relay/) covers each step.

## What Happens If You Don't Meet Requirements

Amazon may reject the application, and in many cases you can reapply. The [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) splits rejection reasons in two:

- **Fixable:** issues "like insurance coverage, authority status, or missing documentation." Amazon says "you're welcome to reapply once it's been addressed."
- **Serious:** some reasons, "such as serious compliance issues," may disqualify you from applying again.

Authority too new? Amazon says "we encourage you to apply early," so it can start reviewing your information before you reach 180 days.

What to check before you apply again is in [Amazon Relay application denied](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-application-denied/). Safety limits are in our [safety score guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-safety-score/).

## After You're Approved

Once your account is active, you can [browse the load board](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/), post your truck for instant matching, and start accepting work. Many carriers use [auto-refresh](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) tools or [auto-booking extensions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) to speed up the process: NudoIQ is designed to work inside the Relay board and give you [lane rate history](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/), net profit per load, and [scorecard dispute assistance](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/).

NudoIQ costs **$49.99 per month** for all features. Start with a **7-day free trial**, no card needed to start, and cancel anytime. **5.0 rating** on the Chrome Web Store. Used by 300+ carriers.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long does Amazon Relay approval take?
Amazon's Relay FAQ says a completed application is typically approved or rejected within 1 to 3 weeks. Our [approval time guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-approval-time/) covers what slows it down and what to do if you hear nothing.

### What if my BASIC score is just slightly over the limit?
Amazon publishes these limits as requirements and doesn't describe any tolerance. For violation limits it says "we won't offer an appeal process." Get under the limit before you apply. See our [safety score guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-safety-score/).

### Can I appeal if my application is rejected?
Amazon doesn't publish an appeal process for applications. Its FAQ says to review the reason for your rejection first, and that you're welcome to reapply once a fixable issue like insurance, authority status or missing documentation is addressed. See [Amazon Relay application denied](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-application-denied/).

### Do I need a business license?
Amazon doesn't list a business license. Its FAQ asks for a DOT number with interstate authority, a valid MC number and a "Carrier" entity type that is "Authorized for Property and for Hire." Check your state for its own registration rules. Amazon does verify your business entity and every owner over 25%.

### Can I use my personal auto insurance?
No. Amazon requires commercial insurance: General Liability, Auto Liability, Cargo and Workers' Compensation. Personal policies don't cover commercial freight work and won't meet Amazon's minimums.

### What if I have a newer authority but all my other metrics are strong?
Relay typically requires your DOT number to be at least 180 days old to complete onboarding, and strong BASIC scores don't replace that (our [new authority guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-new-authority/) has Amazon's exact wording). You can still apply now. Amazon's Relay FAQ says "we encourage you to apply early," so you're ready to move forward as soon as you meet the requirement.

# Amazon Relay Insurance Requirements

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Amazon Relay requires $1,000,000 auto liability per occurrence, $100,000 cargo, and general liability of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate. Semi operators need $50,000 trailer interchange. A lapse blocks booking until coverage is reinstated.

## Insurance is Non-Negotiable

Amazon will not approve your Relay account without proof of insurance. You must provide certificates of insurance (ACORD forms) showing that you meet their minimum limits in all four categories. Your insurance broker or agent can issue these forms.

Insurance costs vary widely based on your carrier's safety record, years in business, equipment type and location. **Do not assume you have enough coverage just because you have an existing policy.** Review your policies now and upgrade if needed before you apply.

## Required Coverages and Limits

| Coverage Type | Minimum Limit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Commercial General Liability | $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate | Covers bodily injury, property damage, personal injury from your operations. The "aggregate" is your total liability across all incidents in a policy year. |
| Auto Liability | $1,000,000 per occurrence | Covers vehicle accidents, third-party injury and property damage. Includes $50,000 trailer replacement (trailer interchange) coverage. |
| Cargo Insurance | At least $100,000 | Covers loss or damage to freight in your trailer or truck while in your care. This protects Amazon's goods during transport. |
| Workers' Compensation | In "all jurisdictions where your company operates" (Relay FAQ) | Covers employee injury or illness from work. Amazon's pages word this two ways; see our [workers' comp guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-workers-comp/). |
| Employer's Liability | $100,000 per occurrence | Part of Workers' Compensation coverage; covers third-party claims related to employee injury. |

## Commercial General Liability: $1,000,000 / $2,000,000

This is your baseline liability protection. It covers bodily injury (someone is hurt because of your operations), property damage (you damage someone's building or equipment), and personal injury (defamation, wrongful eviction, etc.).

**Per Occurrence** means Amazon is covered for up to $1,000,000 on any single incident: a serious accident, a cargo spill, a load that causes property damage.

**Aggregate** means across all incidents in a 12-month policy period, your total liability coverage is $2,000,000. Once you hit that cap, you're self-insured for additional claims until your policy renews.

For a carrier, this is foundational. If you cause a multi-vehicle accident, the other parties' medical bills, vehicle repairs and lost wages can easily exceed $1,000,000. Without this limit, you're liable for everything out of pocket.

## Auto Liability: $1,000,000 with $50,000 Trailer Interchange

Auto Liability specifically covers vehicle accidents and third-party claims related to your truck or trailer.

The **$50,000 trailer interchange coverage** is a specific requirement. This covers damage to trailers you're pulling that don't belong to you. If you're pulling a trailer you don't own and you damage it (backing into a dock, overturning on a curve), trailer interchange coverage pays for repairs up to your policy limit. Amazon requires at least $50,000 for semi operators because the majority of Relay loads are power only: you bring the tractor and pull an Amazon-owned trailer.

If your current auto policy doesn't explicitly list "$50,000 trailer interchange," contact your broker and ask them to add it.

## Cargo Insurance: At Least $100,000

Cargo coverage protects Amazon's freight while it's in your truck or trailer. If cargo is damaged, lost, stolen or contaminated during transport, cargo insurance covers it up to your limit.

$100,000 is Amazon's minimum. This covers most single loads. However, if you're hauling especially high-value freight (electronics, machinery, pharmaceuticals), confirm that a $100,000 limit is sufficient. You can purchase higher limits if needed ($250,000, $500,000 or $1,000,000) at higher premiums.

Cargo claims can happen:
- Load shifts during transit and is damaged.
- Trailer is involved in an accident; goods are destroyed.
- Cargo is stolen from an unsecured truck.
- Refrigerated goods spoil if your reefer unit fails.

Without cargo coverage, you pay the shipper (Amazon, in most Relay cases) out of pocket.

## Workers' Compensation and Employer's Liability

Amazon's [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) asks for workers' compensation "in all jurisdictions where your company operates" and employer's liability of at least $100,000 per occurrence. Its insurance post says "Companies with W-2 employees" need it. Amazon doesn't say how it treats a company with no W-2 employees.

State rules differ too. What Amazon and two states say, and how to ask Amazon, is in our [Amazon Relay workers' comp guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-workers-comp/).

## What Goes on Your Certificate

Your certificate of insurance (ACORD form) needs to show every required coverage and limit. Ask your broker to match the certificate to the requirements listed in your Relay account, and check relay.amazon.com if you're unsure how Amazon wants it worded.

## How to Get the Right Insurance

**Step 1: Gather Your Current Policies**
Pull out your auto and liability policies and review the limits. Write down what you currently carry.

**Step 2: Compare to Amazon's Minimums**
Check if your current coverage meets Amazon's thresholds:
- General Liability: $1M/$2M?
- Auto Liability: $1M with $50K trailer interchange?
- Cargo: $100K minimum?
- Workers' Comp: Compliant with your state?

**Step 3: Contact Your Broker**
If you're short on any limit, call your insurance broker or agent. Tell them you need to meet Amazon Relay's minimums. They'll:
- Quote higher limits if needed.
- Add trailer interchange coverage to your auto policy.
- Issue an ACORD certificate listing the correct limits.

**Step 4: Upload to Your Relay Account**
Once you have certificates showing all four coverages at Amazon's minimums, upload them during your [Amazon Relay sign-up](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

## Insurance Cost Considerations

Insurance premiums depend on several factors:
- Your carrier's safety record and claims history.
- Years in business and driver experience.
- Equipment type (box truck vs. tractor-trailer).
- Geographic territory and annual mileage.
- Your state's workers' compensation classification.

**There is no standard "Amazon Relay insurance" price.** Two carriers with the same trucks can pay vastly different premiums based on their track record. A new carrier with no history will pay more than an established carrier with a clean record.

**Do not call Amazon for premium quotes or rate recommendations.** Contact a commercial truck insurance broker who works with owner-operators. Many specialize in this market and can find competitive rates.

## What Happens After You're Approved

Once you're approved, keep coverage current. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-insurance-requirements) that if your coverage lapses, your company can't book or haul Relay loads until it's reinstated. Renew two to three weeks before your policy expires so RMIS can update your records, and add the updated details in the Insurance tab of your Relay account at least 5 days before the policy expires.

Many carriers use [Amazon Relay auto-refresh](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) tools and [auto-booking extensions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) to streamline load booking. If you want to add lane rate history, net profit analysis and [scorecard dispute assistance](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/), NudoIQ integrates into the Relay board and costs **$49.99 per month**. Start with a **7-day free trial**, no card needed to start, and cancel anytime. **5.0 rating** on the Chrome Web Store. Used by 300+ carriers.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does Amazon Relay insurance cost?
It varies widely based on your safety record, years in business, equipment and location. Request quotes from commercial trucking insurance brokers who work with owner-operators.

### Can I use my personal auto insurance for Amazon Relay?
No. Personal auto policies exclude commercial freight work. You must use commercial auto insurance and commercial liability coverage.

### What if I fall short on one limit?
Contact your broker and upgrade that coverage before applying. Amazon requires each coverage that applies to you at the stated minimums (for workers' comp, Amazon's pages word the rule two ways; see our [workers' comp guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-workers-comp/)).

### Do I need cargo insurance for every load?
If you carry Amazon Relay loads, yes. Your cargo policy should cover all freight you haul on Relay. The $100,000 minimum is usually sufficient; check your policy to confirm.

### What is "trailer interchange" and why does Amazon require it?
Trailer interchange covers damage to trailers you pull that don't belong to you. If you hit a dock or overturn, interchange coverage pays for repairs instead of you.

### Can I increase my cargo limit above $100,000?
Yes. If you frequently haul high-value freight, ask your broker to increase your cargo limit to $250,000, $500,000 or higher.

# Amazon Relay for Box Trucks

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Amazon Relay accepts 16 ft and 26 ft dock-height box trucks with a working tuck-under liftgate, but not cargo vans. Box truck carriers need a DOT number active at least 180 days, a valid MC number and Relay's insurance minimums.

## Box Truck Equipment Specs

Amazon's box truck requirements are precise:

- **16 ft box truck** with a working tuck-under liftgate
- **26 ft box truck** with a working tuck-under liftgate
- The liftgate is required: Amazon will not accept a box truck without one

**Cargo vans are not supported.** That includes sprinter vans and Ford Transit vans. Amazon says cargo vans can't be used on Relay.

Amazon lists these box trucks as dock height (straight truck) with a working tuck-under liftgate. It doesn't explain the reason on its requirements page, so treat the liftgate as a hard requirement and check relay.amazon.com for current specs.

## Box Truck Load Availability

Amazon describes several kinds of box truck work:

- **One-Way Loads**: Amazon says one-way loads will most likely need a box truck or your own trailer.
- **Spot Loads**: Last-minute loads you book right away on the board.
- **Contracts**: Box truck contracts include 8-hour and 13-hour solo contracts with round trips.
- **Post A Truck**: Amazon lists box trucks as eligible, so you can post availability with a minimum rate per mile.
- **Peak Seasons**: Amazon says load volume nearly doubles during Prime Day and the holidays.

Amazon doesn't publish how box truck volume or pay compares with tractor-trailer freight. For more on getting loads, see our guide to [Amazon Relay box truck loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck-loads/).

## Finding Box Truck Loads on the Board

When you log into the [Amazon Relay load board](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/), you'll filter by equipment type. Set the equipment type filter to the box truck size you run, and the board shows only loads that your equipment can haul.

Good loads disappear in seconds. This is why many box truck carriers use [auto-refresh tools](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) or [auto-booking extensions](https://nudoiq.com/best-amazon-relay-extensions/):

- **Refresher Extension**: Automatically reload the board on an interval you set so you see new loads sooner.
- **Alert Mode**: Get an alert when a load that meets your minimums appears.
- **Auto-Book Mode**: Automatically book a load if it meets your minimums, such as load pay or pay per mile.

Even with an extension, competition is fierce. A good rate at a convenient time can book within seconds. That's why many box truck carriers add a refresher or alerts.

## Rate Variability for Box Trucks

[Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) a Relay rate shows a base rate, a fuel surcharge that tracks fuel prices, and tolls. What moves it:

**Distance**
Including deadhead and trip direction.

**Equipment Type and Availability**
What's available in the market for your kind of truck.

**Load Characteristics**
For example, live loads.

**Seasonal Demand**
Amazon says load volume nearly doubles during peak periods like Prime Day and the holidays.

**Regional Market Conditions**
What's happening in the area you pick up from and deliver to.

Amazon Relay does not publish "typical" box truck rates because they vary so much. Check the board yourself during your target hours and see what's posting. A rate that's good one day might be soft the next.

## The Economics of Box Truck Work

To evaluate whether a Relay load makes sense, you need to calculate net profit:

**Gross Rate** (what Amazon pays) minus **Fuel**, **Maintenance**, **Deadhead to Pickup** = **Net Profit**.

On every load, calculate the posted rate minus your estimated fuel, maintenance and deadhead costs. The remainder is your profit for that run. Many carriers set a **profit floor**: the minimum net profit below which they won't take a load. This protects you from unprofitable work.

[Amazon Relay auto-booker](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) extensions like NudoIQ let you set a profit floor automatically. They calculate net profit on every load and only book if it meets your minimum. This removes the guesswork and prevents low-margin mistakes.

## Advantages of Running a Box Truck on Relay

- **Listed Prices**: Spot loads show an all-in price you can book as listed. On select urgent loads, top-performing carriers can name a price through Relay Assistant, and Post A Truck lets you set a minimum rate per mile.
- **Several Ways to Get Work**: The board, contracts and Post A Truck all work for box trucks.
- **Weekly Pay**: Loads completed by 11:59 pm Saturday are paid the following Friday. Invoices are automatic.
- **Set Shift Lengths**: Box truck contracts come in 8-hour and 13-hour solo versions, so you can plan your week.

## Disadvantages and Challenges

- **Rate Swings**: Rates move with distance, season, region and load type, so the same lane can pay differently.
- **Board Competition**: You're competing with other box truck carriers for the same loads. Speed and automation matter.
- **Limited Deadhead**: If you're far from the pickup, the deadhead eats into profit.
- **Scorecard Pressure**: Amazon grades on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free, and your score is the lowest of the four. Late loads and cancellations can pull your grade down and limit access to contracts and early loads. See our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/).

## Getting Started with a Box Truck on Relay

1. **Confirm [Equipment Requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/)**: You have a 16 ft or 26 ft box truck with a working tuck-under liftgate.
2. **Meet [Amazon's Eligibility Requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/)**: DOT authority active for at least 180 days, valid MC number, an acceptable safety rating and BASIC scores, [insurance minimums](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/).
3. **Sign Up at relay.amazon.com**: Submit your application and insurance certificates.
4. **Set Up Your Account**: Invite your drivers (each needs their own Relay profile) and add your equipment.
5. **Start Browsing the Load Board**: Log in, filter by your equipment type, and refresh to see available loads.
6. **Consider an [Auto-Refresh Tool](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/)**: To keep up with competition, many carriers use an extension to refresh the board automatically and get alerts when new loads post.
7. **Set Your Profit Floor and Rules**: If using an [auto-booking extension](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/), configure your minimum net profit and max-books cap.

Driving without a CDL? Read [Amazon Relay non-CDL](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-non-cdl/) for the weight rule and the DOT medical card Amazon still requires.

## Using NudoIQ with Your Box Truck

NudoIQ is designed for carriers on Amazon Relay. It works with [box trucks](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck/), tractors, trailers and containers.

NudoIQ features that help box truck carriers:

- **Auto-Refresh**: Reload the board on an interval you set.
- **Auto-Book with Rules**: Book loads that clear your Min Net Profit and Min $/Mile, up to your max-books cap.

- **Instant Book**: Book from the control bar in one click instead of the multi-step Relay process.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a DOT number to run a box truck on Amazon Relay?
Yes. Amazon requires a DOT number with interstate authority (active for at least 180 days), an MC number, and acceptable safety ratings and BASIC scores. You cannot apply as a gig driver or without formal carrier authority.

### Can I use a sprinter van or Ford Transit?
No. Amazon does not accept cargo vans or small commercial vans. Only 16 ft and 26 ft box trucks with a tuck-under liftgate qualify.

### What if my box truck doesn't have a liftgate?
Amazon requires a working tuck-under liftgate on 16 ft and 26 ft box trucks. Without one, the truck doesn't meet Relay's equipment rules, so install one before you apply.

### What's the typical pay for a box truck load?
It varies by lane, season and time. You must calculate net profit on each load individually (posted rate minus your fuel, maintenance and deadhead costs) to know if it's worth accepting.

### How many box truck loads can I book in a day?
As many as the board offers and you want to accept. It depends on your setup and profit targets. NudoIQ lets you set a max-books cap so you don't over-commit.

### Is it worth running Relay if I'm far from Amazon facilities?
Depends on your location. If you're near a major Amazon distribution center, loads will be available and deadhead costs will be reasonable. If you're very far from the nearest facility, deadhead costs might make most loads unprofitable.

# How Much Does Amazon Relay Pay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-23.

Short answer: Amazon Relay pay varies by load, and Amazon does not publish typical rates. Each rate includes a base rate, a fuel surcharge and tolls. Amazon pays weekly, and loads finished by 11:59 pm Saturday are paid the following Friday.

## What Sets Amazon Relay Rates

Amazon Relay pricing is dynamic. No two loads are priced identically. Several factors influence the posted rate:

The fuel surcharge is already inside the posted price, and here's [how the Amazon Relay fuel surcharge works](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-fuel-surcharge/).

**Season**
The loads and rates you see change through the year. Amazon's [rates guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) says "Seasonal demand fluctuations and regional market conditions will still impact the rates." Its [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) says the board hosts thousands of loads at any given time, nearly doubling in volume when shopping is in full swing, such as Prime Day and the holidays.

**Time of Day**
When a load posts and picks up can change its price. Amazon doesn't publish which hours pay more, so watch your own lanes.

**Origin and Destination**
Different lanes have different characteristics. Where you're picking up and delivering affects what Amazon offers, and Amazon says distance, including deadhead and trip direction, is part of the price. Regional market conditions and load characteristics (for example, live loads) matter too.

**Equipment Type**
Amazon lists equipment type and availability as a rate factor, using reefer as an example. It doesn't publish rate comparisons between equipment types.

**Your Performance Grade**
Your grade changes access, not the posted price. Amazon gives A+, A and B+ carriers early access to new spot loads, and it doesn't say a grade changes what a load pays. Cancelling loads you booked lowers your acceptance score, which can pull your grade down.

**Daily Volume on the Board**
How much freight is on the board that day affects what you see and what it pays. Amazon doesn't publish day-of-week or hour-by-hour patterns.

**Booking Timing**
The moment a good load posts, it typically books within seconds. If you're not actively refreshing or using an auto-refresh tool, you'll miss premium loads and see older, less attractive freight. This is why [auto-refresh extensions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) are widespread among Relay carriers.

## Why the Same Lane Pays Differently Hour to Hour

Here's a made-up example to show how it can play out:

**Tuesday, 6:00 AM**: A load posts from Distribution Center A to Hub B. Amazon posts it at a certain rate. It books within seconds.

**Tuesday, 11:00 AM**: Another load posts: same origin, same destination, same equipment type, same distance. Amazon posts it at a lower rate. This load sits longer because carriers are less interested.

Why the difference? Amazon doesn't say. It publishes no pricing logic for individual loads. Its [rates guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) says "Rates fluctuate. Demand shifts." and names the factors: distance (including deadhead and trip direction), equipment type and availability, load details such as live loads, and seasonal and regional market conditions. How those mix on a given morning isn't public.

The point: there's no "typical" rate for a lane. Rates change constantly, even for the same route. Each posting is independent.

## Weekly Payment Cycle

Amazon Relay pays weekly, regardless of rate:

- **Payment Period**: Sunday 12:00 AM through Saturday 11:59 PM
- **Payment Date**: The following Friday
- **Invoice Generation**: Automatic: no manual invoicing required
- **Pay Disputes**: Submitted through the Amazon Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice

Weekly pay on a set schedule is one of Amazon Relay's consistent advantages.

Our [Amazon Relay payments guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-payments/) covers the weekly schedule, invoices and what to do when pay looks wrong.

Thinking about factoring? See [Amazon Relay factoring and quick pay](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-factoring/).

## How to Judge Whether a Rate Is Good

Since rates vary constantly and there's no industry benchmark, how do you know if a posted rate is worth accepting?

If a rate looks too low to run, here's [why Amazon Relay rates are so low](https://nudoiq.com/why-are-amazon-relay-rates-so-low/) and the levers Amazon gives you.

**Calculate Your True Cost**

A posted rate is gross revenue, not profit. To know if a load is worth your time:

1. Start with the posted rate.
2. Subtract your estimated fuel cost for the round trip.
3. Subtract vehicle maintenance (tire wear, oil, parts depreciation).
4. Subtract deadhead miles to the pickup location (if you're not already positioned there).
5. What's left is your potential net profit.

The formula is straightforward: Posted rate minus your fuel, maintenance and deadhead costs equals your net profit. The same distance can yield different profits depending on your costs and positioning.

To check one load before you book, try our [free Relay load calculator](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-load-calculator/), which shows the net, net per loaded mile and break-even rate.

**Set a Personal Profit Floor**

Many carriers set a minimum net profit they require below which they decline a load. This prevents low-margin work and protects your revenue.

NudoIQ calculates net profit on every load card and lets you set a profit floor. It hides loads below your threshold and won't autobook under it.

**Check Lane History**

If you've run a lane before, you know its typical rate range. If a lane is posted below its usual range, it's a soft day for that route. You can decline and wait for a better rate, or accept if you need volume.

If you're new to a lane, you have no history. [Lane Intelligence](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) tools (like NudoIQ) track posted rates on every lane over 90 days. They show you the target price, historical range and confidence level. This helps you know if a posted rate is strong or soft compared to history.

**Consider the Positioning**

If you're already at or near the pickup location, you can accept lower rates because you have zero deadhead. If you're far from the pickup, deadhead costs will eat into your margin and may make the load unprofitable.

**Know When to Refresh**

Amazon doesn't publish which hours pay best. Track your own lanes by time of day, and use alerts so you see new loads when they post.

## Factors That DON'T Affect Your Rate

**Your Safety Rating or BASIC Score**
Amazon doesn't publish any rate premium for a clean safety record. Your safety record decides whether you can haul at all, and your performance grade affects which loads you see first.

**Your Equipment's Age or Condition**
Amazon publishes nothing that ties a rate to how old or well kept your equipment is. What it does publish are equipment requirements, such as valid CARB certificates for trucks running California loads, which are checked at check-in.

**Haggling on Spot Loads**
Spot loads book at the listed price. The ways to set your own price are Post A Truck (a minimum rate per mile), auctions (bids on contracts up to 6 months, most needing a C+ grade) and Relay Assistant (naming a price on eligible urgent loads, for top-performing carriers; Amazon may counter).

## Pay Disputes and 30-Day Deadline

If a payment looks wrong, [Amazon's Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says you can submit a payment dispute "directly through Amazon Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice." Amazon doesn't publish what proof it wants or how long a review takes, so check each invoice against the pay breakdown you saw at booking and file soon if something's off.

Pay disputes and scorecard disputes are separate. A pay dispute is about money owed, and you file it in the Relay portal. On your scorecard, Amazon publishes dispute language only for on-time impacts, and no dispute route for rejected loads. More in our [Amazon Relay disputes guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-disputes/).

## Understanding Rate Variability

The takeaway: Amazon Relay does not publish "typical" or "average" rates because they vary so much by lane, time, season and carrier profile. Rates on the same route can fluctuate significantly day to day. Don't chase a single good rate you saw yesterday: instead, build a system (auto-refresh, profit floor, lane history) to evaluate each load individually and decide if it's worth your costs.

Many carriers use [auto-refresh](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) tools or [auto-booking extensions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) to remove emotion and speed from the decision. If you want [lane rate history](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/), net profit calculation and [scorecard dispute assistance](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) built into the board, NudoIQ integrates into Relay and costs **$49.99 per month** for all features. Start with a **7-day free trial**, no card needed to start, and cancel anytime. **5.0 rating** on the Chrome Web Store. Used by 300+ carriers.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much money can I make on Amazon Relay?
There's no typical earning amount because rates vary so much by lane, season, time of day and your costs. Calculate net profit load-by-load and decide if each one meets your minimum. Some days you'll see good rates; other days you won't.

### Are rates higher in the morning or evening?
Amazon doesn't publish which hours pay more. Rates move with demand, so the same lane can pay differently at different times. Track your own lanes to see the pattern.

### Can I negotiate a rate with Amazon?
Not on most spot loads, which book at the listed price. On select urgent loads, top-performing carriers can name a price through Relay Assistant, and Amazon may approve or counter. Post A Truck lets you set a minimum rate per mile, and auctions let you bid on contracts.

### Do owner-operators make more than small fleet carriers?
Amazon doesn't publish anything that ties pay to fleet size, and there's no fleet size requirement to haul for Relay. Your performance grade decides access to things like contracts and early spot loads, and auction eligibility also considers equipment count, tenure and CARB compliance.

### How long does it take to get paid after I complete a load?
Amazon's Relay FAQ says the payment cycle runs weekly from Sunday to Saturday, and everything completed before 23:59 Saturday is paid out the following Friday. A load completed after that cutoff isn't in that week's batch.

### What if I dispute a load's rate?
Amazon's Relay FAQ says you can submit a payment dispute through the Amazon Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice. Explain why you think the amount is wrong. Amazon reviews it and decides.

# Is Amazon Relay Worth It?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/is-amazon-relay-worth-it/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Amazon Relay can be worth it if you want weekly pay, steady loads and listed spot prices with no haggling. The trade-offs are speed competition and rates that change by lane and hour. It depends on your costs.

## The Case For Amazon Relay

**Fast Weekly Pay**
Amazon pays weekly: loads completed by 11:59 pm Saturday are paid the following Friday, and invoices are generated automatically. No waiting weeks for a broker to collect money and remit it. No invoices chasing or payment disputes with small shippers. Reliable, predictable cash flow is huge for carriers with tight margins or limited working capital.

**Steady Load Supply**
[Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) the board has thousands of loads at any time, and volume nearly doubles during peak periods like Prime Day and the holidays. This predictability is especially valuable if you want to plan your week or commit to regular routes.

**No Haggling**
Spot loads show an all-in price (base rate, fuel surcharge and tolls) and you book at that price. If you want to set your own number, Post A Truck takes a minimum rate per mile, auctions take bids on contracts, and Relay Assistant lets top-performing carriers name a price on eligible urgent loads.

**National Scale**
Carriers hauling Amazon freight are spread across the country. In our [FMCSA inspection data](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/), California, Ohio, Illinois, Pennsylvania and Texas have the most carriers with Amazon-shipper inspections since 2025. Read it as a floor: an inspection isn't a load, and Amazon freight isn't always booked through Relay.

**Performance Transparency**
Your grade gives you clear feedback on what Amazon measures: on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free. Your score is the lowest of the four, and Amazon gives you a daily prediction of your upcoming score. You know exactly what hurts you and what helps you. Some carriers prefer this clarity over the mystery of traditional brokers.

## The Case Against Amazon Relay

The trade-offs are speed competition for good loads, rates that change by lane and hour, and a performance score that controls access to contracts and early loads.

**Speed Competition**
Good loads book within seconds. If you're manually refreshing the board every few minutes, you'll almost never catch premium freight. You need either hyper-responsiveness or an [auto-refresh tool](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) to stay competitive. This is not passive income; it's active speed competition.

**Rate Volatility**
The same lane can pay very differently on different days. This unpredictability makes it hard to forecast income or plan operating margins. You have to evaluate every load individually and be prepared to decline most of them if they don't meet your profit floor.

**Scorecard Pressure**
Your overall score is the lowest of four metrics, so one weak area sets the grade. Cancellations hurt more the closer they are to pickup, and dropping below C+ can cost you contracts you already booked. See our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/).

**Deadhead Reality**
If you're not already positioned near a pickup, deadhead costs eat into profit. Loads can post far from where your truck sits, and driving there empty wipes out margin.

**Limited Negotiation**
Most spot loads book at the listed price. Outside Post A Truck, auctions and Relay Assistant (for top-performing carriers), a load priced below what you need is a decline.

**No Broker Relationship**
On a traditional freight board, you might build a relationship with a dispatcher who knows your equipment and calls you first with good loads. On Relay, your grade does that job: A+, A and B+ carriers see new spot loads first.

**Rating and Review Visibility**
Your grade lives in your Relay account and decides what you can access. Lower grades lose access to contracts, auctions and early spot loads. Relay's system is metric-based and tied directly to your access.

## Who Relay Works For

Amazon Relay works best for carriers who:

- **Want predictability**. Weekly pay and a busy board matter more to you than hunting for the single best load.
- **Are disciplined about on-time delivery**. If you consistently pick up and drop on schedule, your scorecard stays strong and you keep load access.
- **Can use automation**. [Auto-refresh tools](https://nudoiq.com/best-amazon-relay-extensions/) and [auto-booking extensions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) remove the speed disadvantage and help you set minimums (like a profit floor) instead of manually deciding every load.
- **Are positioned near Amazon facilities**. If you're close to a major distribution center, deadhead is reasonable and loads are plentiful.
- **Have the right equipment**. Amazon says the majority of Relay loads are [power only](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/), so a tractor alone covers most work. Box trucks (16 or 26 ft with a liftgate) can also take one-way loads.
- **Want simple operations**. No customer relations, no multi-week disputes, no contract negotiations. Book, haul, deliver, get paid.

## Who Relay Doesn't Work For

Amazon Relay is a poor fit if you:

- **Often need to cancel booked loads**. The acceptance metric tracks cancellations, including loads that expire, and the penalty grows the closer you are to pickup.
- **Can't absorb rate swings**. Prices move with distance, season, region and load type, which is hard on high-overhead operations.
- **Don't want to use tools**. Without an [auto-refresh tool](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) or alerts, you'll be reloading the board by hand against carriers who use them.
- **Are far from Amazon distribution**. If you're far from the nearest Amazon facility, deadhead costs make most loads unprofitable.
- **Need specialized freight**. Relay supports tractors, 16 and 26 ft box trucks, dry vans, reefers and high-cube containers, so freight that needs other equipment isn't a fit.
- **Want a consistent per-mile rate**. If rate variability stresses you or makes forecasting impossible, Relay's dynamic pricing is a bad fit.

If you don't run trucks, compare Amazon's other programs in [Amazon Relay vs Amazon Flex](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-vs-amazon-flex/).

## The Honest Trade-Off

Amazon Relay rewards **consistency** more than **rate hunting**. You trade a set rate for weekly pay and a busy board. You trade flexibility for clear metrics. You trade personal relationships for a metric-based grade.

If you're a carrier who wants to show up, book loads, deliver on time, and get paid weekly without chasing invoices, Relay can work. If you're a carrier who wants to chase premium loads, negotiate rates, and maintain relationships with brokers, Relay feels limiting.

## How Automation Changes the Equation

[Auto-refresh tools](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) and [auto-booking extensions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) change how Relay feels day to day. With automation:

- You see new loads sooner instead of reloading by hand.
- You set your minimums (like a profit floor) and let the tool do the repetitive work.
- You reduce manual decision fatigue and focus on exceptions.

Without automation, Relay feels like a constant speed race and you'll miss good freight. With it, Relay becomes a manageable, repeatable system.

These testimonials reflect carriers who found value in [load booking tools](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) and [dispute assistance](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/).

## Final Answer: Is It Worth It?

**For volume-focused carriers with strong on-time performance and access to Amazon facilities**: Yes. The steady work and fast pay are valuable.

**For carriers who need rate negotiation, flexibility, or long-haul work**: No. You'll be frustrated by Relay's fixed pricing and regional focus.

**For carriers who are currently on Relay but frustrated**: Likely yes, but only if you adopt automation. An [auto-refresh tool](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) and [rate/profit intelligence](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) can make Relay easier to manage.

Start with the [7-day free trial](https://nudoiq.com/best-amazon-relay-extensions/) of an extension. See how it feels to run with automation. If you spend less time hunting and more time keeping your scorecard clean, it's probably worth staying. If you're still frustrated by rate variability or competing for premium loads, Relay might not be your channel.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do most carriers make money on Amazon Relay?
Amazon doesn't publish carrier profit data, and we don't either. Whether it works depends on your costs, location, equipment and discipline. Your net profit per load, after driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead, is what decides it.

### Can I run Relay part-time?
Yes. You set your availability and accept or decline loads as you choose. But the acceptance metric tracks cancellations of loads you booked, so book only what you can run.

### What's the biggest pain point for Relay carriers?
The speed competition for good loads and rate variability are the two biggest complaints. Refreshers and booking rules help with speed, and lane history and net profit help with judging rates.

### Should I quit my broker and switch to Relay full-time?
Not necessarily. Relay can be one channel alongside other freight. Amazon's freight is only on Relay, but not every lane or shipper is Amazon.

### Is Relay harder to manage than a traditional freight board?
No, it's actually simpler. With a freight board, you hunt for loads and negotiate. With Relay, loads are published, spot prices are listed, and invoices are automatic. The trade-off is less control and less negotiation.

### How do I know if I have the right equipment for Relay?
Check the [equipment requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/). Day cab, sleeper, box truck (16/26 ft with liftgate), reefer, dry van and containers all work. Cargo vans don't.
