# How do you post a truck on Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-post-a-truck/
Published: 2026-10-08. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Create a Post A Truck order with your availability (up to two weeks ahead), a pickup radius and maximum deadhead, and your minimum rate per mile. Relay matches loads to the order and books them for you.

## What is Post A Truck on Amazon Relay?

Post A Truck is the opposite of searching the board. You post your equipment and driver availability, set the least you'll take, and Relay brings matching loads to you. [Amazon's Post A Truck guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck) says matched carriers get first access to freight in their window, before it reaches the load board.

Amazon also says it will [instantly book loads that match your criteria](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-to-find-truck-loads-faster-with-amazon-relays-free-freight-search), so you don't have to watch the board. That's the upside and the risk in one sentence: whatever matches is yours to run.

## Who can use Post A Truck?

Amazon says approved Relay carriers can access it. Beyond that:

- **Equipment.** [Amazon lists](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/booking-options/3-ways-to-set-your-own-freight-rates-on-amazon-relay) power only loads, box trucks (dock height and liftgate required) and live loads using your own tractor-trailer.
- **Grades.** Every grade keeps Post A Truck. Higher grades get priority matching. Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explains how grades work.
- **Account.** You need an approved carrier account first. See the [Amazon Relay requirements checklist](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

## How do you post a truck on Amazon Relay, step by step?

Amazon's guides describe what goes into an order rather than a screen-by-screen path. These are the choices an order asks you to make, in a sensible order to work through them.

1. **Pick how you start.** From scratch, from recommendations, or from a saved search (see the next section).
2. **Set your availability.** The days and hours your truck and driver are free, up to two weeks in advance.
3. **Set where the first pickup can be.** A radius for first pickup and a maximum deadhead.
4. **Choose destinations.** Include or exclude cities, and add preferred destinations.
5. **Pick one-way or round trip.** A round trip brings you back. A one-way will most likely need a box truck or your own trailer.
6. **Set distance or trip duration limits** so a match fits your driver's day.
7. **Set maximum stops and stem time.**
8. **Set your price.** Your minimum rate per mile and a payout amount.
9. **Check the match outlook**, adjust if it's Low, and post the order.

You can create several orders for different trucks and lanes, and edit or cancel them any time.

## What are the three ways to start an order?

| Way to start | How it works |
|---|---|
| From scratch | You fill in every setting yourself |
| From recommendations | You enter a few settings and Relay fills the rest from your previous bookings |
| From a saved search | A search you saved on the board becomes the template |

If you already have a saved search for your home lane, starting from it is the fastest way to post.

## What do High, Medium and Low match outlook mean?

Match outlook is Relay's estimate of how likely your order is to match. It's based on your criteria and the previous 6 weeks of loads.

| Outlook | What Amazon says | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| High | Good chance of a match | Post it |
| Medium | Decent chance, room to improve | Loosen one setting if timing matters |
| Low | Adjust radius, distance, destination or price | Change one of those and check again |

Amazon says matching also uses market rates and Relay performance scores. Narrow criteria give fewer matches, and flexibility on routes or timing can help. So price isn't the only lever: Amazon lists radius, distance and destination right next to it.

## What are linked orders and block orders?

They solve two different problems.

- **Linked orders** connect several orders as one fulfilled order, so you don't overbook the same truck. Once one is fulfilled, the unfulfilled trips are cancelled for you.
- **Block orders** have trips that start and end at the same location. A matched block is paid in full even if Amazon doesn't use the entire block length. Blocks are explained in our guide to [Amazon Relay contracts and blocks](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contracts/).

If you post one truck on several lanes at once, linked orders are the setting that keeps you from matching twice.

## What happens when your order matches?

An order stays open until it matches or your availability window expires. Amazon's general rule for booked loads is plain. In [Amazon's words](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-performance-score), "if an Amazon load is booked, it's the Relay carrier's responsibility to execute it."

Rejecting a booked load counts against your acceptance metric, and the closer to pickup, the higher the penalty. Our guide on [what happens if you cancel a load](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cancel-load/) covers it.

## How do you cancel a Post A Truck order?

Amazon says you can cancel an order if your availability changes, and edit or cancel orders any time. Do it as soon as plans change. An open order with the wrong hours can match a load your driver can't run, and then you're cancelling a booked load instead of an order.

If you're using Post A Truck to chain work after a delivery, our guide to [booking multiple loads on Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/how-to-book-multiple-loads-on-amazon-relay/) walks through the hours math first.

## How does NudoIQ's One-Click Post A Truck work?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs inside your signed-in Relay load board tab. It's an independent tool, not made by or affiliated with Amazon. It adds a row of buttons under each load card, and the third one opens One-Click Post A Truck.

The panel shows that load's origin, destination, distance and board price next to your minimum rate per mile and minimum payout. Above the price field sits a recommended bid, based on what that lane has paid before.

Be clear on one thing: the recommended bid is not accurate right after install. It needs time gathering data about your area, and it improves with use. Treat it as a starting point and set your own price.

When the price is right, click Post Truck Now and an order is created for that load automatically. You skip building the order from a blank form.

If you use LoadFetcher, see [how its Post Truck Manager compares](https://nudoiq.com/loadfetcher-alternative/) with One-Click Post A Truck.

NudoIQ is used by 300+ carriers. Try it with a 7-day free trial, and cancel anytime. It's rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### How far ahead can you post a truck on Amazon Relay?
Up to two weeks ahead. The order stays open until it matches or your availability window expires.

### Can box trucks use Post A Truck on Amazon Relay?
Yes. Amazon lists box trucks as eligible, as long as the truck is dock height with a liftgate. Power only loads and live loads with your own tractor-trailer are eligible too.

### Why is my Post A Truck match outlook low?
Low means your criteria don't line up well with the loads Relay saw in the previous 6 weeks. Amazon suggests adjusting your radius, distance, destination or price. More flexibility on routes or timing can help.

### Does Post A Truck guarantee a load?
No. Your order only books if a load matches it before your availability window ends. Higher grades get priority matching, and matching also weighs market rates.

### Can I post more than one truck on Amazon Relay?
Yes. You can create several orders for different trucks and lanes. Use linked orders when one truck is posted on more than one order, so unfulfilled trips are cancelled once one fills.

### Does Post A Truck work for power only?
Yes. Amazon lists power only loads as eligible. Choose round trip if you don't have your own trailer, because one-way loads will most likely need a box truck or your own trailer.

---

# What happens if you cancel a load on Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cancel-load/
Published: 2026-10-08. Last updated: 2026-10-23.

Short answer: Cancelling (rejecting) a load you booked counts against your acceptance metric, and Amazon says the closer to pickup you reject, the higher the penalty. Your overall score equals your lowest metric, so it can lower your grade.

## What counts as a cancellation on Amazon Relay?

Amazon calls it a rejection. Its [performance score guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-performance-score) defines the acceptance metric as "How often a carrier rejects loads that they book." Amazon's [grades page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) says the same thing in other words: booking and completing loads without rejections, meaning carrier cancellations.

Two things count:

- **Rejecting a load you booked.** Any time you give a tendered load back, your score can take a hit.
- **Letting a booked load expire.** Amazon says this counts too. Doing nothing isn't a way out.

Amazon is plain about who owns a booking: "if an Amazon load is booked, it's the Relay carrier's responsibility to execute it."

## Does it matter when you cancel?

Yes, a lot. Amazon says: "The closer a carrier rejects to pick-up time, the higher the penalty."

The practical rule is simple. The moment you know a load won't work, release it. A cancellation two days out costs less than the same cancellation two hours out. Amazon doesn't publish how much less, but it does say the penalty rises as pickup gets closer.

## What if Amazon cancels the load?

Then it doesn't count against you. Amazon says that if it cancels tendered loads, the carrier's performance score won't be impacted.

What Amazon does and doesn't publish about pay on a load it cancels is in our [Amazon Relay TONU guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-tonu/).

You also don't lose the time completely. Amazon's [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) says the board suggests replacements for cancelled loads. Check the pickup window, deadhead and your driver's hours before you take one.

## How does one cancellation affect your whole grade?

Your overall score equals your lowest metric. Amazon scores four: on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free. If acceptance is your weakest, it sets your grade, even with a perfect on-time record.

You become eligible for a grade after ten or more Relay loads in the last six active weeks. Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) breaks down all four metrics.

## What does a lower grade cost you?

Access. Here's what Amazon says each grade level gets you:

| Grade | What Amazon ties to it |
|---|---|
| All grades | Load board access, Relay Rewards eligibility, Post A Truck (higher grades get priority matching) |
| C+ and up | Most freight auctions (B for reefer, B+ for some box truck loads) |
| B and up | Seeing and booking new contracts |
| A+, A and B+ | Early access to new spot loads |
| A+ and A | Contract price alerts |
| Below C+ | Contracts you already booked are at risk |

Relay Rewards uses your lowest score too. Amazon evaluates your tier monthly, using your company's lowest score from the previous month. So a bad stretch on acceptance can reach past this week's loads into contracts, auctions and rewards. Our guides to [Amazon Relay contracts](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contracts/) and [auctions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auctions/) explain what's on the line in each.

## How do you avoid having to cancel?

Amazon's own advice is to be selective when you browse the load board, so you don't book loads you can't haul. In practice:

1. **Do the hours math before you book.** First load, deadhead and second load against your driver's remaining hours. Our guide to [booking multiple loads](https://nudoiq.com/how-to-book-multiple-loads-on-amazon-relay/) has a checklist.
2. **Check the pickup window, not just the price.** Can your driver make it with room to spare?
3. **Use linked orders in Post A Truck.** If one truck is posted on several orders, linking them means unfulfilled trips are cancelled for you once one fills. See [how to post a truck on Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-post-a-truck/).
4. **Keep your Post A Truck availability current.** Cancel an order the moment plans change, before it matches a load.
5. **Release early when you must.** The penalty rises as pickup gets closer.

## What doesn't Amazon publish about cancellations?

More than most carriers expect. Amazon doesn't publish:

- **Cancellation fees.** The [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says nothing about cancellation fees, or about pay when a truck order isn't used.
- **The size of the penalty** for a single rejection.
- **How long one cancellation stays** on your score. Amazon says the score reflects your last six weeks of hauls.
- **The score cutoffs** for each letter grade.
- **A dispute route for acceptance.** Amazon's dispute language on the performance score page covers on-time impacts only. It doesn't describe a way to dispute an acceptance hit.

If someone quotes you exact numbers for any of these, ask where they got them.

Our [Amazon Relay disputes guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-disputes/) covers each dispute type and what Amazon publishes about it.

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs inside your signed-in Relay load board tab. It's an independent tool, not made by or affiliated with Amazon. It doesn't change how Amazon scores a rejection. What it does is let you set rules up front about which loads get booked at all.

In Autobook mode it's set to book only loads that clear rules you set:

- **Min Net Profit.** It books only loads that clear your own minimum net profit.
- **Complete data.** It never books a load with incomplete data.
- **Max-books cap.** It stops after the number of bookings you set.

If you'd rather decide every load yourself, Alert mode tells you about a match without booking it. More in our [auto-booker guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/).

Comparing auto bookers for your trucks? Here's [whether Load Fetcher auto books loads](https://nudoiq.com/loadfetcher-alternative/), going by its own listing and plans.

Try it with a 7-day free trial, and cancel anytime. NudoIQ is rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does rejecting a load on Amazon Relay hurt your score?
Yes. Rejecting a load you booked counts against your acceptance metric, and the closer to pickup you reject, the higher the penalty. Because your overall score is your lowest metric, acceptance can set your whole grade.

### Is there a fee for cancelling an Amazon Relay load?
Amazon doesn't publish one. The Relay FAQ says nothing about cancellation fees. The cost Amazon does describe is to your performance score.

### What happens if Amazon cancels my Relay load?
Your score isn't affected. Amazon says carrier scores aren't impacted when it cancels tendered loads, and the load board suggests replacements for cancelled loads.

### Does letting a load expire count as a rejection on Amazon Relay?
Yes. Amazon says a performance score can take a hit any time a carrier rejects tendered loads, including letting loads expire.

### Can I dispute an acceptance hit on my Relay scorecard?
Amazon doesn't publish a dispute route for acceptance. Its dispute language covers on-time impacts. For account-access problems, Amazon's FAQ points to the Support Center when you're logged in. The 24/7 Relay Operations Center handles operational support through the Relay portal or Relay mobile.

### How long does a cancellation stay on my Amazon Relay score?
Amazon doesn't say how long a single cancellation stays. It says your score reflects your last six weeks of hauls.

# Can you use a cargo van for Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cargo-van/
Published: 2026-10-08. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: No, you can't. Amazon's truck requirements page says "Cargo vans cannot be used for loads on Amazon Relay." The smallest equipment Amazon supports is a 16 ft dock-height box truck with a working tuck-under liftgate.

## What does Amazon say about cargo vans on Relay?

Amazon says it in one line on its [truck requirements page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-truck-requirements): "Cargo vans cannot be used for loads on Amazon Relay." The [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) lists the same equipment and no vans.

So there's no van category to apply under, and no van loads to book. It doesn't matter how big the van is or how much it can carry. If it's a cargo van, it's out.

## What equipment does Amazon Relay accept?

This is Amazon's full supported list:

- **Tractors:** day cabs (short-distance) and sleeper cabs (long haul).
- **Box trucks:** 26 ft and 16 ft, dock height (also called straight trucks), with a functional tuck-under liftgate.
- **Trailers:** 48 ft trailers, 53 ft dry vans and 53 ft reefers. Reefers must meet the FDA Sanitary Transportation Rule.
- **Containers:** 20, 40 and 45 ft high cube, UIIA compliant, for drayage from rail and sea ports.

Two more things from the same page. Most Relay loads are power only: you bring the tractor and Relay supplies the trailer. And there's no fleet size requirement, so one truck can be enough.

## Can you use a sprinter van, pickup or hotshot for Amazon Relay?

Not on the list. Amazon's page doesn't name sprinter vans, pickup trucks or hotshot rigs at all. It lists what's supported, and none of them are on it.

So if you run a hotshot or a pickup today, that rig isn't on the list Amazon supports. Plan around equipment that is.

No CDL? See what Amazon says about non-CDL box trucks in [Amazon Relay non-CDL](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-non-cdl/).

## What does FMCSA data show about trucks hauling Amazon freight?

In roadside inspections, big trucks carry almost all of it. We counted public FMCSA roadside inspections that list Amazon as the shipper, from 2023-09-24 to 2026-09-22. Of the 100,499 inspection rows with a vehicle weight class:

| Vehicle weight class | Share of Amazon-shipper rows |
|---|---|
| Over 54,000 lb (tractor-trailer) | 87.7% |
| 33,001 to 54,000 lb | 2.5% |
| 19,501 to 26,000 lb (box truck) | 7.4% |
| 14,001 to 19,500 lb | 0.7% |
| 10,001 to 14,000 lb | 0.1% |
| 10,000 lb or less | 0.0% |

At the carrier level, among carriers inspected with Amazon freight since 2025-01-01: tractor-trailer 83.9%, box truck 13.3%, step van 0.3%, and van 14,000 lb or less 0.1%.

Two caveats. An inspection is not a load: most loads are never inspected, so these counts are a floor. And Amazon on the bill of lading means Amazon freight, not proof of a Relay booking. It includes Amazon's own fleets and contract carriers. The full method is on our [Amazon Relay carrier data page](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/).

## If you own a cargo van, what are your options for Relay?

Three paths exist, and each one starts with supported equipment.

### Run a box truck

A 16 ft or 26 ft dock-height box truck with a working tuck-under liftgate is the smallest way in. Box trucks can book spot loads, one-way loads and contracts, including 8-hour and 13-hour solo contracts with round trips. Our [Amazon Relay box truck guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck/) covers the truck, and [how Amazon Relay contracts work](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contracts/) covers booking weeks of work ahead.

### Rent the equipment

Amazon says "Discounts are available for renting box trucks and tractors for a load." The terms are on [Amazon's discounts page](https://relay.amazon.com/discounts), so check them there before you plan around a rental.

### Go power only with a tractor

Most Relay loads are power only. A day cab or sleeper tractor hooks to an Amazon trailer, so you don't need to own a trailer for most of the work. Read [how Amazon Relay power only works](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/).

Amazon Flex, a separate Amazon program, accepts vans for package delivery. See [Amazon Relay vs Amazon Flex](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-vs-amazon-flex/).

## What else do you need besides the right truck?

The equipment is only one gate. The carrier account has its own rules, and they're the same whatever truck you run:

- A DOT number with interstate authority, active for at least 180 days, and a valid MC number.
- An FMCSA safety rating of Satisfactory, None or Not Rated.
- Insurance, including $1,000,000 auto liability per occurrence and at least $100,000 cargo.
- Verification of the business and every beneficial owner (anyone with more than 25%).

The full checklist is in our [Amazon Relay requirements guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/), with coverages in the [insurance requirements guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/).

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

Straight answer: NudoIQ can't help a cargo van get on Relay. There are no Relay loads for vans, so there's nothing for it to find.

Once you run supported equipment and have an approved Relay account, it's useful on the board. NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs inside your signed-in Relay load board tab. It auto refreshes the board, alerts you on box truck or power only loads that match your rules, and shows net profit on every load card after driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead. It's an independent tool, not made by or affiliated with Amazon.

Weighing board tools for later? Here's [what Load Fetcher does and costs](https://nudoiq.com/loadfetcher-alternative/), next to NudoIQ.

When you're ready, try it with a 7-day free trial, and cancel anytime. NudoIQ is rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you use a sprinter van for Amazon Relay?
No. Sprinter vans aren't on Amazon's supported equipment list, and Amazon says cargo vans can't be used for Relay loads. The smallest supported truck is a 16 ft dock-height box truck with a working tuck-under liftgate.

### Can you use a pickup truck for Amazon Relay?
Pickup trucks aren't on Amazon's supported equipment list. What Relay lists is day cab and sleeper tractors, 16 ft and 26 ft dock-height box trucks with a tuck-under liftgate, trailers and high cube containers.

### Can you do Amazon Relay with a hotshot?
Hotshot rigs aren't on Amazon's supported equipment list, so plan on a tractor or a box truck instead. Most Relay loads are power only, which means a day cab or sleeper tractor pulling an Amazon trailer.

### Is there an Amazon Relay load board for cargo vans?
No. Because Amazon says cargo vans can't be used on Relay, there are no van loads on the board. The smallest equipment that gets you onto the board is a 16 ft dock-height box truck with a working tuck-under liftgate.

### What is the smallest truck you can use for Amazon Relay?
A 16 ft box truck. It has to be dock height with a functional tuck-under liftgate. A 26 ft box truck with the same features also qualifies.

### Does Amazon help with renting a truck for Relay?
Amazon says discounts are available for renting box trucks and tractors for a load. The terms are on its discounts page at relay.amazon.com/discounts.

# Why does the Chrome Web Store show fewer users for NudoIQ than 300+ carriers?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/chrome-web-store-user-count/
Published: 2026-10-08. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: The Chrome Web Store only counts installs from NudoIQ's store listing, created on May 21, 2026. Before that, carriers got NudoIQ directly, so they aren't in the store's number. In total, NudoIQ is used by 300+ carriers.

## How carriers got NudoIQ before the store

NudoIQ did not start on the Chrome Web Store. Caleb, who built it, distributed it directly to carriers on Amazon Relay, without the store.

NudoIQ was only recently turned into a Chrome Web Store extension. The store listing was created on May 21, 2026. Carriers who were already using NudoIQ before that date got it outside the store.

## What the store number counts

Google says the user count on a Chrome Web Store listing reflects users of that store item, meaning installs from that listing.

So the number on NudoIQ's listing only covers carriers who installed it through the store. It does not include the carriers who got NudoIQ directly. That is why the user count on the store listing is smaller than the 300+ carriers who use NudoIQ.

Nothing is hidden here. These are two different counts: one from the store, one from everyone using NudoIQ.

## How to check it yourself

Open the [NudoIQ listing on the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/nudoiq/bjilnjgfdndecmamphkkcpplfmniocgk). You will see the user count and the rating. NudoIQ is rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

The most useful check is your own board. NudoIQ starts with a free week, every feature, no card. You start it on your Relay load board. After 7 days, $49.99/month only if you add a card. Cancel anytime. See [pricing](https://nudoiq.com/#pricing).

To see how NudoIQ compares with other Relay extensions, read [why carriers choose NudoIQ](https://nudoiq.com/why-nudoiq/).

NudoIQ is independent and not affiliated with Amazon.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is NudoIQ the best Amazon Relay extension?
Judge it on the facts. NudoIQ is the only Amazon Relay extension that books to your own minimum net profit and drafts scorecard dispute letters, and the only one in our side-by-side that lists all six core features (checked October 5, 2026).

### Does NudoIQ have a free version?
No free plan. NudoIQ starts with a 7-day free week with every feature, and you start it with just your email, no card. After 7 days, it's $49.99 a month only if you add a card. Cancel anytime.

### How much does NudoIQ cost?
$49.99 a month for every feature, the same for one truck or twenty. There is no annual plan, and you can cancel anytime.

### Does NudoIQ work in Spanish?
Yes. The NudoIQ interface is in English and Spanish.

### Is NudoIQ affiliated with Amazon?
No. NudoIQ is an independent extension and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon. It runs in your own signed-in Relay tab and never asks for your Amazon password.

## Rocket Relay alternative FAQ

### What is Rocket Relay?
Rocket Relay is a browser extension for Amazon Relay, published by West Wanted (checked October 9, 2026). NudoIQ is a separate one, with AutoBook at your minimum net profit.

### Is Rocket Relay a Chrome extension?
Yes, it installs from the Chrome Web Store. NudoIQ is a separate Chrome extension. If you try both, run one load board extension at a time so they don't clash.

### Does Rocket Relay have a free trial?
Yes, a 7-day Pro trial. Its FAQ says you add a card to start (checked October 9, 2026). NudoIQ gives you 7 days free, no card needed to start.

### Does Rocket Relay auto book loads?
Yes, on its Pro plan, by your filters such as payout and price per mile (checked October 9, 2026). NudoIQ's AutoBook books only loads that clear your minimum net profit.

### Is Rocket Relay a refresher or an auto booker?
Both. Its listing names auto-refresh and Auto-book, with Auto-book on Pro (checked October 9, 2026). NudoIQ does both too, and AutoBook books only loads that clear your minimum net profit.

### Is Rocket Pro the same as Rocket Relay?
Yes, Rocket Pro is the Rocket Relay extension. Its store listing is named Relay Auto Booker Refresher Rocket Pro. Pro is also its paid plan's name (checked October 9, 2026).

### What is Rocket Relay Post Truck Manager?
A separate Chrome Web Store listing for Post a Truck orders, from Tasiev LLC, not West Wanted (checked October 9, 2026). NudoIQ has One-Click Post A Truck under each load.

### Can I switch from Rocket Relay to NudoIQ?
Yes, in a few minutes. Turn off or remove Rocket Relay, add NudoIQ from the Chrome Web Store and start your 7 days free. Your Relay login stays the same.

### Is NudoIQ or Rocket Relay made by Amazon?
No. NudoIQ is an independent product by Sami Enterprises LLC, not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Amazon. Rocket Relay is published by West Wanted.

### Does NudoIQ work in Spanish?
Yes. NudoIQ's buttons and banners on the load board work in English and Spanish. Telegram messages are in English.

### How does NudoIQ decide which loads to book?
Only loads that clear your Min Net Profit and it can fully price, up to your Max books. Alert mode just alerts. See [what happens if you cancel a load](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cancel-load/).

# Write your Amazon Relay scorecard dispute letter

URL: https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-dispute-letter/
Published: 2026-10-12. Last updated: 2026-10-12.

Free Amazon Relay scorecard dispute letter generator: pick the violation, tick what's true, copy a letter to submit in Relay. Runs in the browser, nothing is sent, and Amazon decides every dispute.

## What a strong Relay dispute letter does

A strong letter makes one argument. Pick the one thing that went wrong on this trip and stay on it. Three loose reasons read like excuses, and the reviewer only needs one that holds up.

Put times in it. "Arrived at the gate at 5:40, cleared at 6:55" says more than "the facility was slow," and Amazon can check it against its own records.

Close with a clear ask. Ask Amazon to review the trip and remove the impact from your score, or to share the record that shows the violation. Either answer tells you where you stand.

## Which reasons usually get denied

Traffic, weather, a DOT or roadside inspection, or the app or phone failing usually get denied when they explain why your truck was late to the pickup or why the app went dark. Attaching more records rarely changes that.

There is one case the tool does argue. If your driver left the pickup on time and heavy traffic or bad weather slowed the drive to a later stop, the letter says so, built on that on-time departure. Otherwise the lines this tool writes leave those reasons out, and if your own notes mention them, it warns you. When something else happened on that trip too, like a held door or a jammed gate, lead with that.

Rejected loads are hard to turn around, and Amazon doesn't publish a dispute route for acceptance. Read how cancelling a Relay load hits your score (https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cancel-load/) before you file one.

## What to gather before you file

Pull these together while they are fresh:

- Check-in or gate times. On-time is measured from check-in, so this comes first.
- App and location records for the trip.
- Messages with Relay support about the load.
- Photos of the gate line, the dock or the site.
- Bills of lading or gate receipts with a time stamp.

Amazon does not publish a deadline for scorecard disputes, so file as soon as you spot the hit. For how the score itself works, see the Amazon Relay scorecard guide (https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Do you have to pay or install anything to use this tool?
It's free, and you don't install anything. It works in the browser on your phone or your computer.

### Is the info you type sent anywhere?
Your trip ID, facility and notes are never sent to us or anyone else. The letter is put together right here in your browser.

### Will this letter get the violation removed from my scorecard?
Nobody can promise you that. Amazon reviews every dispute and makes the call. A short letter with exact times and records makes your side easy to check.

### How do I submit the letter in Relay?
Copy the letter, open your scorecard in Relay and start a dispute on that trip. Paste the letter in, read it once more and submit. Amazon doesn't publish a deadline for scorecard disputes, so file while your records are fresh.

### Can NudoIQ write the dispute letter for you automatically?
You still tick what's true and submit the letter yourself. On your Relay scorecard page, NudoIQ lists the violations it finds and drafts the letter from the facts you tick. Dispute letters come with the 7-day free trial, then it's $49.99/month.

# See what a Relay load nets before you book

URL: https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-load-calculator/
Published: 2026-10-12. Last updated: 2026-10-12.

Free Amazon Relay load calculator: enter pay, loaded and deadhead miles, fuel price, MPG and costs per mile to see the net, net per loaded mile and break-even rate. Runs in the browser.

## How your net is worked out

Start with what the load pays. Then take off what the whole trip costs you, empty miles included. Your truck burns fuel on the way to the pickup and on the way home, so total miles are loaded miles plus deadhead.

From there, the costs are:

- Fuel: total miles divided by your MPG, times the fuel price.
- Other costs: total miles times your other cost per mile.
- Tolls for the trip.

Net is the pay minus those three. Net per loaded mile is that net divided by the loaded miles.

## What the break-even rate tells you

Break-even is your total cost divided by the loaded miles. It is the lowest rate per loaded mile that covers your costs on this load. Below it, the load costs you money to run.

Use it before you book. Compare it with the rate on the board. When the two are close, one long wait at the dock or a detour can wipe out what is left. Set your own floor from your own numbers. See Amazon Relay rates (https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-rates/) for how pricing works.

## Why net per mile beats the posted rate per mile

The posted rate per mile does not know your truck. It leaves out your fuel, your driver pay and the empty miles you drive to get to the pickup.

Two loads can post the same rate and leave you with very different money once deadhead is counted. Net per loaded mile puts every load on the same footing, so you compare what each one leaves you after costs. For what affects pay on Relay, read how much Amazon Relay pays (https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Does deadhead count in the net?
Deadhead counts. It goes into your total miles, so fuel and other costs cover the empty drive to the pickup and back home. Net per mile and break-even are divided by loaded miles, since those are the miles the load pays for.

### What MPG should I use?
Use your truck's average over the last few fill-ups, loaded and empty together. The calculator starts at 9, but box trucks and tractors run very different numbers, so put in your own.

### Is what you type saved or sent anywhere?
Nothing you type is sent anywhere. The math runs in your browser on this page.

### Does NudoIQ show this on the Relay load board?
On your Relay board, NudoIQ shows the net and net per mile under the price on every load card. It works from costs you set once in Settings and counts deadhead to the pickup and the drive home, but not tolls. It runs in Chrome on a computer, and the net shows once you start your no-card free week. After that, $49.99/month only if you add a card.

### What goes in other cost per mile?
Put in everything you pay per mile besides fuel: driver pay, maintenance, tires and insurance, each worked out per mile. If you pay something by the week, like insurance or a truck note, divide it by the miles your truck runs in a normal week.

# Amazon Relay payment schedule: when do carriers get paid?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-payments/
Published: 2026-10-14. Last updated: 2026-10-23.

Short answer: Amazon Relay pays weekly. Its FAQ says the cycle runs Sunday to Saturday, and everything completed before 23:59 Saturday is paid the following Friday. Invoices are generated automatically in the Relay portal.

## When does Amazon Relay pay carriers?

Amazon pays on a weekly cycle. Here is the rule, word for word, from [Amazon's Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq): "Payment cycle runs weekly from Sunday-Saturday. Everything completed before 23:59 Saturday will be paid out the following week on Friday."

So the week closes Saturday night and payday is the Friday after. Amazon's [rates guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) puts it simply: "Amazon pays carriers weekly for completed loads." Contract work runs on the same rhythm. Amazon's [contracts guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-trucking-contracts) says you're paid weekly for all work completed the week before.

## How long does Amazon Relay take to pay?

Amazon calls it 7-day pay. Its [RelayCon 2026 experts post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/industry-trends/freight-industry-insights-from-experts-at-amazons-relaycon-2026) mentions "7-day payment terms and no factoring fees." Its [broker comparison](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/freight-brokers-vs-direct-booking-why-choose-amazon-relay) says "With Relay, you typically get paid within 7 days," and contrasts that with "30-60 day waits for payouts from logistics brokers."

The rule that actually sets your payday is the FAQ one above. Look at which Sunday to Saturday week the load was completed in, then find the Friday after that week. A load completed after 23:59 Saturday isn't in that week's batch.

What Amazon does and doesn't say about factoring is in [Amazon Relay factoring and quick pay](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-factoring/).

## What are Amazon Relay's payment terms?

Here's what Amazon publishes:

- **Weekly cycle.** Sunday to Saturday, paid the following Friday.
- **No invoicing on your end.** The FAQ says "Amazon Relay will generate invoices automatically."
- **Pay shown before you book.** The rates guide says you see the full payout upfront, broken into base rate, fuel surcharge and tolls.
- **No factoring fees.** Amazon's RelayCon 2026 experts post pairs 7-day payment terms with no factoring fees.
- **Bank details at signup.** The [application steps](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-become-a-carrier-for-amazon-relay) end with "Payment information."

Amazon doesn't publish the payment terms in its carrier agreement, the payment method (ACH or check), what time money lands on Friday, or holiday changes to the Friday payout. For what loads pay per mile, see our guide to [how much Amazon Relay pays](https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/).

Thinking about factoring anyway? Read [Amazon Relay factoring and quick pay](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-factoring/) first.

## Where do you see Relay invoices and payment status?

In your company's Relay account. The FAQ says "You will be able to review all invoices and payments in Amazon Relay portal." The rates guide adds that you can track payment status there too.

## What does "payment pending" mean on Amazon Relay?

Amazon doesn't publish what "pending" means or how long it lasts. What you can check yourself:

1. **The completion date.** Was the load completed before 23:59 Saturday? If not, it belongs to a later week.
2. **The invoice.** Open it in the portal and compare it to the base rate, fuel and tolls you saw when you booked.
3. **Fraud checks.** The only cause of a payment delay Amazon names on its public pages is fraud. Its [geospoofing post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-safety/geospoofing-how-amazon-relay-combats-fake-gps-technology) says fake GPS leads to "payment delays during fraud investigations."

## What should you check when an Amazon Relay payment looks wrong?

Amazon doesn't publish a list of common payment issues. These checks come straight from what it does publish:

- **Amount vs. breakdown.** Line up each invoice with the pay breakdown from booking.
- **Loads you didn't haul.** Amazon's geospoofing post says: "Review your invoices to make sure they match loads your company actually hauled." Report fraud to relay-network-reports@amazon.com.
- **Bank account changes.** If your bank details changed and you didn't change them, the FAQ says to report it through the Support Center while logged into your Relay account.

To see what a single load really left you, run it through our [free Relay load calculator](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-load-calculator/). It shows net, net per loaded mile and break-even for one load.

## How do you dispute an Amazon Relay payment?

Through the portal. The FAQ says: "You can submit payment disputes directly through Amazon Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice."

Amazon doesn't publish what proof it wants, how long a review takes, or whether a correction comes in the next pay cycle or separately. So review each invoice the week it posts and file soon if something's off. Our [Amazon Relay disputes guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-disputes/) covers payment disputes next to performance disputes and the other types.

## Does Amazon Relay pay detention, TONU or layover?

Amazon publishes no detention, TONU, layover or lumper policy for Relay. When we checked all 139 pages in Relay's public sitemap on October 14, 2026, none of them used the words "detention" or "layover."

For what to do when Amazon cancels a load you were ready to run, read our [Amazon Relay TONU guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-tonu/).

Here's what Amazon does publish:

- **The price is all-in.** Amazon's [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) says spot loads are "booked at the all-in price listed on Relay's load board. The base rate, fuel surcharges, and tolls charges are included."
- **"Accessorials" means fuel and tolls.** Amazon's [auctions guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/freight-bidding-on-amazon-relays-auctions) says "Accessorials (fuel and tolls) are paid after the load is complete."
- **Fuel surcharge is paid.** The rates guide says it "adjusts based on current fuel prices." Amazon says it's added in accordance with its Relay Program Policies, which aren't public, and it doesn't publish the formula.
- **Blocks pay in full.** The load board guide says "Blocks are typically paid in full even if your drivers and equipment aren't needed." The [Post A Truck guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck) says the same for matched blocks, and the contracts guide says Amazon pays "a competitive rate if the full block of time isn't used."
- **Lumper fees.** Amazon doesn't publish who pays a lumper on a Relay load or how it's reimbursed.

If a load runs late, Amazon's [free freight search post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-to-find-truck-loads-faster-with-amazon-relays-free-freight-search) says you can call the Relay Operations Center "about delays or unexpected changes to a load." Amazon's [hours of service post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-safety/hours-of-service-how-to-comply-with-the-fmcsa) says reporting changes helps your performance score reflect "only the factors within your control." It doesn't say reporting adds pay.

Detention, TONU and layover rates you may see online come from Amazon Freight's shipper terms. Those are charges Amazon Freight bills to shippers, not what Relay pays carriers.

If pay on a delayed or changed load looks wrong, check the breakdown, then use the payment dispute route above. Amazon doesn't say whether that route covers accessorial claims.

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for the Relay load board. It's an independent tool, not affiliated with Amazon. It shows net and net per mile under the price on every load card, from costs you set once, and Lane Intelligence shows a lane's price history. So you know what a load should leave you before you book it, not when the invoice posts. It's free for 7 days with no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month.

## Frequently asked questions

### What day does Amazon Relay pay carriers?
You get paid on Friday. Amazon's Relay FAQ says the payment cycle runs Sunday to Saturday, and everything completed before 23:59 Saturday is paid out the following Friday.

### Do I need to send Amazon Relay an invoice?
You don't have to. Amazon's Relay FAQ says Amazon Relay generates invoices automatically, and you can review all invoices and payments in the Relay portal.

### How long do I have to dispute an Amazon Relay payment?
Amazon's Relay FAQ says you can submit payment disputes through the Amazon Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice. Amazon doesn't publish how long a review takes.

### Does Amazon Relay pay detention?
Amazon doesn't publish a detention policy for Relay, and none of its public Relay pages mention detention. It says spot loads are paid at an all-in price that includes base rate, fuel surcharge and tolls.

### Does Amazon Relay pay a fuel surcharge?
You do get one. Amazon says the load price includes a fuel surcharge that adjusts based on current fuel prices. Amazon points to its Relay Program Policies, which aren't public, and doesn't publish the formula.

### Does Amazon Relay offer quick pay?
Amazon's public Relay pages don't describe a quick pay or early pay option today. The schedule Amazon publishes is weekly, paid the Friday after the Sunday to Saturday week.

# How do you file a dispute on Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-disputes/
Published: 2026-10-14. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Amazon publishes two dispute routes for Relay. Submit payment disputes in the Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice, and let Relay know to dispute on-time score impacts. There's no published route for rejected loads.

## What can you dispute on Amazon Relay?

Less than most carriers expect. Amazon publishes a dispute route for two things: payments and on-time performance. For most other problems it publishes nothing, and for one it says plainly there's no appeal.

| Dispute type | Where Amazon says to file | Published deadline |
|---|---|---|
| Payment | The Amazon Relay portal | 30 days from reviewing your weekly invoice |
| Performance (on-time) | "Let Relay know" (exact menu isn't public) | None published |
| Rejected load (acceptance) | No route published | None |
| Trip completion | Not mentioned anywhere | None |
| Driver verification | No route; Amazon manually reviews failed selfie checks | None |
| Roadside inspection violation limits | No appeal | Not applicable |
| Cargo loss or theft | Relay support center, with documentation | None published |

The exact menu path for every dispute type sits behind the Relay login, so we can't show it here.

## How do you file a payment dispute on Amazon Relay?

In the portal. [Amazon's Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says: "You can submit payment disputes directly through Amazon Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice."

That's the only dispute deadline Amazon publishes. It doesn't say what proof it wants or how long a review takes. Compare each invoice to the base rate, fuel and tolls you saw at booking, and file soon if something's off. Our [Amazon Relay payments guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-payments/) covers the weekly pay cycle and what to check.

## How do you file a performance dispute on Amazon Relay?

Amazon's [performance score guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-performance-score) says, in its on-time section: "If something happens along the way, carriers can let Relay know and dispute performance score impacts." Amazon measures on-time from the check-in timestamp at the site.

Amazon doesn't publish a deadline for performance disputes, what evidence a dispute needs, how long a decision takes, or whether there's a second level of appeal.

The same guide says Relay's support center for onboarded carriers "addresses common scenarios that affect performance scores." In September 2026 Amazon [said](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-amazon-relays-improving-to-support-carrier-growth) it's "now resolving performance disputes 20% faster," without giving a starting point.

Two habits help. Report schedule changes to the Relay Operations Center as they happen. Amazon's [hours of service post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-safety/hours-of-service-how-to-comply-with-the-fmcsa) says that helps your score reflect "only the factors within your control." And don't sit on a dispute, since no deadline is published. Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explains all four metrics. If you need to write one up, our [free Relay dispute letter tool](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-dispute-letter/) lets you tick what's true and copy a letter. Amazon decides.

## Can you dispute a rejected load on Amazon Relay?

Amazon publishes no route for it. The performance score guide says your score "can take a hit any time a carrier rejects tendered loads," and "That includes letting loads expire." Its dispute language covers on-time only.

One thing does work in your favor. If Amazon cancels a tendered load, your score isn't impacted. More in our guide to [cancelling an Amazon Relay load](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cancel-load/).

## Is there a trip completion or driver verification dispute?

Not one Amazon publishes. The phrase "trip completion dispute" appears on no public Relay page. If a trip problem shows up in your pay, the payment dispute route above is the one Amazon documents.

For driver verification, Amazon's [driver eligibility page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/driver-eligibility-requirements-to-haul-amazon-loads) says "Amazon manually reviews unsuccessful selfie checks" and warns that "Multiple failed selfie checks can impact a driver's and carrier's access to Relay." It describes no dispute process. New driver documents (CDL front and back plus a selfie) are typically reviewed within 48 hours.

## What can't you appeal on Amazon Relay?

Roadside inspection violation limits. Amazon's [inspection violations post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-safety/how-amazon-relay-uses-data-about-roadside-inspection-violations) says: "Like BASICs violations, we won't offer an appeal process." Carriers with "three or more inspections that exceed our violation limits may lose access to Relay loads."

## Is there an Amazon Relay dispute phone number?

No. The FAQ says it directly: "Amazon Relay doesn't have an official contact phone number." Our [guide to contacting Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contact/) lists where Amazon sends each problem instead.

## How do you report cargo loss or theft on Relay?

Amazon's [cargo theft post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/cargo-theft-reduce-your-companys-risk) says carriers "must also report loss prevention issues in the Relay support center with relevant documentation, such as a police report."

## What about a legal dispute with Amazon?

The [Conditions of Use](https://relay.amazon.com/terms) on the Relay site send "Any dispute or claim relating in any way to your use of any Amazon Service" to binding arbitration. Those are the general site terms. The carrier agreement itself isn't public.

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for Amazon Relay, an independent tool not affiliated with Amazon. On the Relay scorecard page, it finds the violation and drafts a dispute letter. You check it and submit it, and Amazon decides. On the load board it shows net and net per mile under the price on every load card. It's free for 7 days with no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a phone number for Amazon Relay disputes?
No, Relay has no dispute phone line. Amazon's Relay FAQ says Amazon Relay doesn't have an official contact phone number. Our guide to contacting Amazon Relay lists where Amazon sends each problem.

### Is there a deadline for an Amazon Relay performance dispute?
You won't find one published. The only published dispute deadline is for payment disputes: 30 days from reviewing your weekly invoice. Don't assume that window applies to your score.

### How long does an Amazon Relay performance dispute take?
You won't find a published decision time. In September 2026, Amazon said it is resolving performance disputes 20% faster, without giving a starting point.

### Can I dispute a rejected load on Amazon Relay?
You won't find a published dispute route for acceptance. Rejecting a tendered load, or letting it expire, can lower your score. Loads Amazon cancels don't affect your score.

### Can I appeal Amazon Relay's roadside inspection violation limits?
You can't. Amazon says it won't offer an appeal process for its inspection violation limits, and carriers with three or more inspections over those limits may lose access to Relay loads.

### How do I report cargo theft on Amazon Relay?
Amazon says carriers must report loss prevention issues in the Relay support center with relevant documentation, such as a police report.

# Amazon Relay phone number: how do you contact Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contact/
Published: 2026-10-14. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Amazon's Relay FAQ says there's no official Amazon Relay phone number. For a load in progress, reach the 24/7 Relay Operations Center (ROC) through the Relay portal or app. Account problems go to the Support Center when you're logged in.

## Does Amazon Relay have a phone number?

No. [Amazon's Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says it plainly: "Amazon Relay doesn't have an official contact phone number."

People still search for one, with queries like "amazon relay phone number usa 24 7". No such number is published on relay.amazon.com. Treat any number you find on another site as unverified, and never give it your login.

One wrinkle. Amazon's [free freight search post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-to-find-truck-loads-faster-with-amazon-relays-free-freight-search) says you can "call our operations center" about delays or unexpected changes to a load. It doesn't print a number. So the way in is still the Relay portal or the Relay app.

## Who do you contact for each Relay problem?

| Your problem | Where Amazon sends you |
|---|---|
| A load in progress: delay, change, breakdown | Relay Operations Center (ROC), 24/7, through the Relay portal or Relay mobile |
| A driver needs help on the road | Relay Assistant chat in the Relay app |
| Account access or security | Support Center, when logged into your Relay account |
| Your application | Contact Us, top right of your application page |
| Suspicious activity or double brokering | relay-network-reports@amazon.com |
| A change of ownership | relay-ownership-transfers@amazon.com, at least 30 days ahead |
| Privacy or data request | transportation-privacy@amazon.com |
| A payment that looks wrong | Payment dispute in the Relay portal |
| A life-threatening situation | 911 |

## How do you reach the Relay Operations Center?

Through Relay itself. The FAQ says: "Amazon provides 24/7 operational support for our carriers through the Relay Operations Center (ROC)." It adds that the ROC "can be reached through the Relay portal or Relay mobile."

Report schedule changes as they happen. Amazon's [hours of service post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-safety/hours-of-service-how-to-comply-with-the-fmcsa) says drivers and carriers "can use our app to connect with our operations for support," and that telling operations about a change helps your performance score reflect "only the factors within your control."

Amazon doesn't publish a response time for the ROC. "24/7" is the only service promise on the page.

## How do drivers get help on the road?

In the app. Amazon's [mobile app post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-truckers-use-the-amazon-relay-mobile-app) says drivers can "request support from Relay Assistant throughout their trip," an AI chat tool for problems out on the road. "If they have a breakdown or mechanical issue, they can report it in the app."

The chat isn't a dead end. Amazon's [September 2026 update](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-amazon-relays-improving-to-support-carrier-growth) says: "When Relay Assistant can't resolve an issue, it connects you to a human operator with your conversation's full context."

## Who do you contact about your Relay account?

The Support Center. For account security, the FAQ says to "reach out to us through the Support Center when logged into your Relay account."

Can't log in at all? Our [Amazon Relay login guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-login/) walks through Amazon's reset steps and how to spot a fake login page. If your account is suspended rather than locked, our [account suspended guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-account-suspended/) covers what to check.

## Who do you contact about an application?

Use Contact Us. The FAQ says to contact Relay support "by clicking Contact Us on the top right of your application page."

Before you do, check your FMCSA record. Amazon's onboarding team reaches applicants using the contact information on file with FMCSA. If that doesn't match your application, its messages can miss you.

## How do you report fraud or double brokering?

By email. The FAQ says to "email relay-network-reports@amazon.com with a detailed description of the suspicious activity, including the DOT #s involved."

If you've been a victim of fraud, Amazon's [geospoofing post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-safety/geospoofing-how-amazon-relay-combats-fake-gps-technology) also says to "file a report with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) at reportfraud.ftc.gov and your local law enforcement agency."

Check the address bar too. Amazon's [email scams post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/email-scams-how-to-spot-a-fake) says legitimate Relay websites have "relay.amazon.com" at the beginning of the URL.

## Who handles ownership changes and privacy requests?

* **Ownership changes.** The email scams post says to "email relay-ownership-transfers@amazon.com at least 30 days ahead."
* **Privacy and data requests.** The FAQ says to contact transportation-privacy@amazon.com.

What Amazon says about buying or selling a Relay carrier is in [Amazon Relay business for sale](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-business-for-sale/).

## Who do you contact about pay or a scorecard hit?

Pay problems go through the portal. The FAQ says you can submit payment disputes "directly through Amazon Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice." Our [Amazon Relay disputes guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-disputes/) lists each dispute type and where Amazon says to file it.

For a late arrival or app usage hit you think is wrong, our [free Relay dispute letter tool](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-dispute-letter/) lets you tick what's true and copy a letter to submit. Amazon decides.

## Do Relay Rewards carriers get faster support?

Amazon's [Relay Rewards post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-carriers-save-with-relay-rewards) lists "Dedicated office hours" with "priority assistance from Amazon Relay's support team" among the program's benefits. It doesn't say which tier gets them or publish the hours. That post says the program is US only, though relay.amazon.ca also lists "Rewards and Discounts" without details.

In Canada, relay.amazon.ca gives the same ROC answer: it's reached through the Relay portal or Relay mobile.

## What doesn't Amazon publish about contacting Relay?

* Any phone number, for the US, Canada or "24/7" support
* ROC hours beyond "24/7," or any response time
* A route for someone fully locked out, beyond the account recovery steps
* A mailing address for carriers
* A dispute phone number

If a site gives you a number for any of these, it didn't come from Amazon's Relay pages.

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for the Relay load board, an independent tool not affiliated with Amazon, so it's not a way to reach Amazon support. On your Relay scorecard page it drafts a dispute letter from the violation, and you check it and submit it. Amazon decides. On the board it shows net and net per mile under the price on every load card, free for 7 days with no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there an Amazon Relay customer service phone number?
No, Amazon Relay has no customer service line. Amazon's Relay FAQ says Amazon Relay doesn't have an official contact phone number. Load problems go to the 24/7 Relay Operations Center through the Relay portal or Relay mobile, and account problems go to the Support Center when you're logged in.

### What is the Amazon Relay ROC phone number?
Amazon doesn't publish a number for the Relay Operations Center. Its FAQ says the Relay Operations Center (ROC) gives 24/7 support and is reached through the Relay portal or Relay mobile. Treat any ROC number on a third-party site as unverified.

### What is the Amazon Relay support email?
Amazon Relay publishes no general support email. The emails it does publish are for specific jobs: relay-network-reports@amazon.com for suspicious activity, relay-ownership-transfers@amazon.com for ownership changes and transportation-privacy@amazon.com for privacy requests. Account help goes through the Support Center while logged in.

### Is there an Amazon Relay phone number for drivers?
No, drivers get help in the Relay app. They can chat with Relay Assistant during a trip and report breakdowns there, and Amazon says Relay Assistant connects them to a human operator when it can't resolve an issue.

### What is the Amazon Relay contact number in Canada?
Amazon doesn't publish a Relay phone number for Canada. The relay.amazon.ca page says the 24/7 Relay Operations Center is reached through the Relay portal or Relay mobile, the same as in the US.

### How do I contact Amazon Relay about my application?
Click Contact Us on the top right of your application page, as Amazon's FAQ says. If you haven't heard back in two weeks, first check that your FMCSA contact information matches your application exactly, since Amazon's onboarding team uses it to reach you.

# How long does it take to get approved for Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-approval-time/
Published: 2026-10-14. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Amazon's Relay FAQ says a completed application is typically approved or rejected within 1 to 3 weeks, and delays come from validating insurance. If you hear nothing after two weeks, check that your FMCSA contact information matches your application exactly.

## How long does Amazon Relay approval take?

Usually one to three weeks. [Amazon's Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says that once Amazon receives your completed application, "it will typically be approved or rejected within 1-3 weeks."

Amazon's own pages don't all give the same range, though:

| Amazon page | What it says |
|---|---|
| [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) | Approved or rejected within 1 to 3 weeks |
| [How to become a carrier](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-become-a-carrier-for-amazon-relay) | "Amazon generally reviews completed applications within three weeks." |
| [Prime Day post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-news-events/prime-day-for-amazon-relay-carriers) | Approval "can take 2-3 weeks" |
| [High volume events post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-news-events/best-practices-for-amazons-high-volume-events) | "about 1-3 weeks" |

So plan on up to three weeks. And note the word "completed." The clock starts when Amazon has everything, not when you open the form.

Filling out the form is the quick part. Amazon's carrier post says you can submit everything "in as little as 20 minutes." You'll give your DOT number and company details, verify a one-time password, list your equipment and add payment information. What you need to qualify is in our [Amazon Relay requirements guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

In Canada it's faster on paper. The relay.amazon.ca page says applications are approved or rejected within 2 to 4 business days.

For each application step in Amazon's order, see [how to sign up for Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/how-to-sign-up-for-amazon-relay/).

## What slows a Relay application down?

Insurance, by Amazon's own account. The FAQ says: "Delays, if any, will be due to validation of insurance information."

What Amazon tells you to do about it:

* **Have it all ready first.** Amazon "urges you to have all data ready prior to applying."
* **Call your insurance provider if it stalls.** The FAQ says to reach out to them in the event of any delays.
* **Get your insurance on file with FMCSA.** If your insurance gets flagged, Amazon says to "ensure your provider submits the information directly to FMCSA."
* **Give new insurance time.** If you're already a Relay carrier and changing insurance, the high volume events post recommends allowing 2 weeks for it to process.

Our [insurance requirements guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/) lists the minimums your certificate needs to show.

## Can you apply before your DOT number is 180 days old?

Yes. The FAQ says Relay "typically requires your DOT number to be at least 180 days old to complete onboarding," but "we encourage you to apply early."

Amazon words the 180-day rule four ways. Our [new authority guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-new-authority/) puts them side by side.

## Haven't heard back after two weeks?

Check your FMCSA record first. The FAQ says to check "that your FMCSA contact information matches your Relay application details, down to the dash or comma."

That detail matters because "Our onboarding team uses your information on file with the FMCSA to reach you." If the phone number or email on file is old, Amazon's messages may never reach you.

If everything matches and you still haven't heard, click Contact Us on the top right of your application page. The FAQ also says Amazon Relay doesn't have an official contact phone number, so don't go looking for one.

You can watch progress from your phone. Amazon's carrier post says to "download the Relay app on iOS or Android to get started and track your application's progress on the go."

## Can you reapply if Amazon Relay rejects your application?

Often, yes. The FAQ says: "In many cases, you may be eligible to reapply." Fixable reasons like insurance, authority status or missing documents can be addressed first, while serious compliance issues may disqualify you.

What to check before you apply again is in [Amazon Relay application denied](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-application-denied/).

## What happens after you're approved?

The FAQ says you'll get an email with instructions to access your Relay account. Then:

1. **Complete the Relay 101 course** in Relay's Learning Center (about 10 minutes).
2. **Add your drivers and equipment** to your Relay profile. Each driver is invited and verified separately.
3. **Start booking** through the Relay load board.

Before the first booking, work out what a load leaves you. Our [free Relay load calculator](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-load-calculator/) takes a load's pay and miles and shows your net and net per loaded mile, deadhead included.

## What doesn't Amazon publish about approval?

* What each application status, such as "in review," means
* Any way to speed up a review
* A waiting period before you reapply
* A full list of rejection reasons
* An approval rate

If someone promises a faster approval, ask where that's written on relay.amazon.com.

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

Once you're approved, the load board is where the work starts. NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for the Relay load board, an independent tool not affiliated with Amazon. It shows net and net per mile under the price on every load card, from costs you set once, and Lane Intelligence (the first button under a load) shows that lane's price history. It's free for 7 days with no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long does Amazon Relay take to approve an application?
Amazon's Relay FAQ says a completed application is typically approved or rejected within 1 to 3 weeks. Other Amazon posts say within three weeks or 2 to 3 weeks, so plan on up to three. Delays come from insurance validation.

### How do I check my Amazon Relay application status?
Amazon says you can track your application's progress in the Relay app on iOS or Android. It doesn't publish what each status means. If you hear nothing in two weeks, check your FMCSA contact details, then click Contact Us on your application page.

### Why was my Amazon Relay application rejected?
Amazon tells you to start with the rejection reason it gives you. Its FAQ names insurance coverage, authority status and missing documentation as fixable reasons, and says serious compliance issues may disqualify you from applying again. Amazon doesn't publish a full list. See [Amazon Relay application denied](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-application-denied/).

### Can I reapply to Amazon Relay after a rejection?
In many cases, you can. Amazon's FAQ says you're welcome to reapply once a fixable issue like insurance coverage, authority status or missing documentation is addressed. It publishes no waiting period.

### Does Amazon Relay accept new authority?
Relay typically requires your DOT number to be at least 180 days old to complete onboarding. Amazon's FAQ still encourages you to apply early, so it can start reviewing your information before you meet the requirement, and our [new authority guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-new-authority/) has its exact wording.

### How long does Amazon Relay approval take in Canada?
The relay.amazon.ca page says Canadian applications are approved or rejected within 2 to 4 business days, with any delay due to insurance validation.

# Amazon Relay background check: what drivers and carriers should know

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-background-check/
Published: 2026-10-14. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Every driver onboarding to Amazon Relay must meet standardized background check requirements before hauling Relay loads. Amazon's approved provider runs the check from the driver's Relay app and looks for past criminal or motor vehicle record violations.

## How does a driver get onboarded to Amazon Relay?

By invitation. [Amazon's Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says: "A carrier needs to invite their drivers to create a profile in the Relay app." Amazon's [driver eligibility post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/driver-eligibility-requirements-to-haul-amazon-loads) adds that drivers can't share their accounts.

The driver downloads the Relay app on iOS or Android and logs in to an Amazon account, or creates one. Then they enter their commercial driver's license and contact details. Two checks follow: an identity check and a background check. Our [dispatcher guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-dispatcher/) covers the invite steps from the dispatch side.

If you're a driver looking for a way in, start with [Amazon Relay for drivers](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-drivers/).

## What does the identity check involve?

A license and a selfie. The FAQ says drivers "complete identity verification by submitting a selfie and a photo of their driver's license." The driver eligibility post says Amazon verifies the license front and back, and that "Amazon typically reviews the information within 48 hours."

Only drivers who pass the identity check can haul Relay loads.

## What does the Amazon Relay background check look at?

The FAQ says "all drivers onboarding to Relay must meet standardized background check requirements before hauling Amazon Relay loads."

Here's what Amazon says about how it works:

* **It starts in the app.** The background check kicks off during onboarding in the driver's Relay app.
* **Amazon picks the provider.** "Amazon works with our approved background check provider to look for past criminal or motor vehicle record violations."
* **Outside checks don't count.** "We won't approve checks supplied by other providers."

Amazon doesn't name the provider on its public pages.

## How long does the Amazon Relay background check take?

Amazon doesn't say. The only time it publishes is the 48-hour review for the identity check. Nothing on relay.amazon.com gives a time for the background check itself.

Amazon also doesn't explain the statuses drivers search for, like "in review," "overdue" or "verification due." So give yourself room. Invite a new driver well before you plan to put them on a load.

## Can you do Amazon Relay with a felony?

Amazon doesn't publish an answer. It says the check looks for "past criminal or motor vehicle record violations," but it doesn't list which offenses disqualify a driver or how far back the check goes.

Anyone who gives you a firm yes or no isn't quoting Amazon. The honest path is to have the driver go through onboarding and see the result.

## Why does the Relay app ask drivers for selfies during loads?

To confirm the right driver is on the load. The driver eligibility post says Relay uses facial recognition at specific times during loads. The app requests periodic selfies, "for example, at pickup and/or drop-off," and matches them to the selfie from onboarding.

What Amazon says happens next:

* "Amazon manually reviews unsuccessful selfie checks."
* "Multiple failed selfie checks can impact a driver's and carrier's access to Relay."
* Drivers can decline, but "this will prevent them from hauling Relay loads."

Amazon's [secure freight page](https://relay.amazon.com/pages/secure-freight-how-amazon-prevents-trucking-fraud-theft) says facilities use "driver's license validation and real-time photo verification" so only authorized drivers get in.



## Can you dispute a failed selfie or background check?

Amazon publishes no dispute route for either. Manual review of failed selfie checks is the only step it describes. Our [Amazon Relay disputes guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-disputes/) lists the routes Amazon does publish.

If a hold-up at the gate turns into a late arrival hit on your scorecard, that's an on-time issue, and Amazon does let carriers dispute on-time impacts. Our [free Relay dispute letter tool](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-dispute-letter/) lets you tick what's true and copy a letter to submit. Amazon decides.

## What if a driver's license photo keeps getting rejected?

Amazon doesn't publish its photo rules or why a photo fails. Here's what it does say:

- Drivers submit "a selfie and a photo of their driver's license," and Amazon checks the license front and back.
- "Amazon typically reviews the information within 48 hours."
- Amazon's FAQ points account security issues to the Support Center "when logged into your Relay account," and it's Relay's support route for onboarded carriers. There's no phone line.

So stop resubmitting the same photo. Open a Support Center ticket from the carrier's Relay account, attach a screenshot of each rejection and ask Amazon to name what fails. Amazon doesn't publish how many retries a driver gets.

## What is the carrier responsible for?

More than Amazon's checks. The driver eligibility post says "Relay-approved carriers are independent contractors, not Amazon employees. Carriers are responsible for their own drivers."

Amazon lists what that covers: carriers manage "drug and alcohol screening, hours of service (HOS) compliance, medical certification," plus regular license checks and ongoing driver qualification.

And one rule to put in writing for your dispatch desk: "Carriers should only assign Amazon loads to drivers who have successfully passed background checks and drug screenings" that meet or exceed federal rules.

## Do carrier owners get verified too?

Yes, through a separate check. The FAQ says carrier identity verification confirms "your business entity and the identity of all beneficial owners (anyone with more than 25% ownership)."

In its answer about carrier owners, the FAQ says Amazon may keep Facial Recognition Information for up to 30 days after it's generated, or longer for fraud detection or investigation, but not more than one year.

Amazon's [get started page](https://relay.amazon.com/get-started) points owners to the Persona Privacy Policy for details on how Persona processes their information.

## What doesn't Amazon publish about background checks?

* The background check provider's name
* How far back the check goes
* Which offenses disqualify a driver
* How long the background check takes
* An appeal or dispute process for a failed check
* What statuses like "verification due" or "asset verification" mean

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ has no part in driver checks. Those stay between your drivers and Amazon. It's an independent Chrome extension for the Relay load board, not affiliated with Amazon, that shows net and net per mile under the price on every load card and drafts scorecard dispute letters you check and submit. It's free for 7 days with no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long does the Amazon Relay background check take?
Amazon doesn't publish a time for the driver background check. The only time it gives is for the identity check, which Amazon typically reviews within 48 hours. Invite new drivers well before you need them on a load.

### How far back does the Amazon Relay background check go?
Amazon doesn't say how far back a driver's check goes. Its driver eligibility post says the check looks for past criminal or motor vehicle record violations, but it publishes no look-back period.

### Can you do Amazon Relay with a felony?
Amazon doesn't publish which offenses disqualify a driver. It says only that its approved provider looks for past criminal or motor vehicle record violations. The driver has to go through onboarding to get an answer.

### What are the Amazon Relay background check requirements?
Every driver onboarding to Relay must meet standardized background check requirements before hauling loads. The check starts in the driver's Relay app and is run by Amazon's approved provider, and Amazon won't approve checks from other providers.

### What is Amazon Relay driver verification?
It's the identity check every driver completes when onboarding: a photo of the driver's license, front and back, and a selfie. Amazon typically reviews it within 48 hours. During loads, the Relay app also asks for periodic selfies, for example at pickup or drop-off.

### What does Amazon Relay background check in review mean?
Amazon doesn't explain driver background check statuses on any public page, and it publishes no route for status questions. Our suggestion: start with the Support Center while logged in, the channel Amazon names for account and security issues, since Amazon publishes no phone number.
