# Does Amazon Relay require workers' comp?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-workers-comp/
Published: 2026-10-16. Last updated: 2026-10-16.

Short answer: Yes, Amazon Relay lists it. The FAQ asks for workers' compensation "in all jurisdictions where your company operates" and employer's liability of at least $100,000 per occurrence. Amazon's insurance post says companies with W-2 employees need it.

## Does Amazon Relay require workers' comp?

Yes, it's on Amazon's list. The [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) asks for:

- "Workers' compensation insurance in all jurisdictions where your company operates"
- "Employer liability not less than $100,000 per occurrence"

Amazon's [insurance requirements post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-insurance-requirements) says it another way: "Companies with W-2 employees need Workers' Compensation meeting state guidelines and $100,000 in Employers Liability per occurrence."

## Why do Amazon's two wordings matter?

They aren't the same rule.

| Amazon page | Who it covers |
|---|---|
| Relay FAQ | "all jurisdictions where your company operates" |
| Insurance post | "Companies with W-2 employees" |

The FAQ names no exception for a company with no employees. The post ties the rule to W-2 employees. Amazon doesn't say which one wins.

Amazon also says "Carriers employ their own drivers." They work for you, not Amazon.

## Do owner-operators with no employees need workers' comp?

Amazon doesn't say. Neither Relay page covers a one-truck company with no employees. That leaves two questions:

1. **Your state.** Does state law make you carry it? See below.
2. **Amazon.** What will Relay accept from your company? Ask Amazon before you apply.

## What do state rules say?

Each state sets its own. Two examples:

**Florida** ([Division of Workers' Compensation](https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/coverage-requirements)):

- Outside construction, "Employers with four (4) or more employees, including business owners who are corporate officers or Limited Liability Company (LLC) members, must have workers' compensation coverage."
- Sole proprietors and partners outside construction "are not employees" unless they choose to be covered.
- "Out-of-state employers must notify their insurance carrier that they are working in Florida."

Not sure which class you're in? Florida points you to the National Council on Compensation Insurance at (800) 622-4123.

**Texas** ([Texas Department of Insurance](https://www.tdi.texas.gov/wc/employer/index.html)): "private employers can choose to carry workers' compensation insurance coverage, but it is not required in most cases."

Another state? Ask your state's workers' comp agency. State law tells you what the law asks, not what Relay accepts.

## Does a Florida workers' comp exemption count for Relay?

Amazon doesn't publish whether it accepts any state exemption.

Here's what Florida says an [exemption](https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/wc/employer/exemptions) is. It lets corporate officers and LLC members "exclude themselves as employees." Exemptions go to those officers and members, "not to the business."

So an exemption applies to you, the officer, and takes you out of coverage. Florida says an exempt officer "may not recover workers' compensation benefits." It doesn't apply to the drivers you hire. Ask Amazon what it accepts before you count on one.

## How does Amazon check your coverage?

Through your certificate of insurance. Amazon's insurance post says: "You submit your current insurance details when you apply to Relay. Then our third-party vendor gets the COI from your company's agent, broker, or insurance company on file."

- **At application.** The FAQ says delays "will be due to validation of insurance information."
- **Flagged policy.** Work with your provider until it meets Amazon's minimums, then "ensure your provider submits the information directly to FMCSA."
- **Renewals.** Amazon says to renew "at least two to three weeks before your expiration date." A lapse stops booking. See [how to fix an insurance lapse](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-account-suspended/).

## How do you ask Amazon about workers' comp?

- **Applying?** Amazon's FAQ points applicants to Contact Us on the top right of the application page.
- **No phone.** The FAQ says "Amazon Relay doesn't have an official contact phone number."
- **Other routes.** Our [Relay contact guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contact/) lists where Amazon sends each kind of question.

Ask one plain question: what does Relay accept for workers' comp from your company, in your state? Keep the answer in writing.

Once you're onboarded, Amazon's insurance post says it offers onboarded Relay carriers competitive quotes through McGriff Insurance on coverage that meets Amazon's requirements. See our [rewards guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-rewards/).

Other minimums: [insurance requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/).

## What doesn't Amazon publish about workers' comp?

- Whether it accepts a state exemption certificate
- Whether a company with no W-2 employees, or only 1099 drivers, must show workers' comp
- How it treats Texas employers that don't carry it
- Whether occupational accident insurance can stand in for it
- Which states "where your company operates" covers
- The certificate wording it wants

This isn't legal or insurance advice. Confirm with Amazon, your state agency and your agent.

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

Once your coverage clears and you're booking, NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for the Relay load board. It shows net profit on each load from costs you set once, driver pay included. It's independent, not affiliated with Amazon, and it never asks for your Amazon password. Try it 7 days free, no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month. [See how the NudoIQ extension works](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-chrome-extension/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Amazon Relay require workers' comp for owner-operators?
Amazon doesn't say how it treats a company with no employees. Its FAQ asks for workers' comp in all jurisdictions where your company operates, while its insurance post ties the rule to companies with W-2 employees. Ask Amazon before you apply.

### How much employer's liability does Amazon Relay require?
$100,000 per occurrence. Both the Relay FAQ and Amazon's insurance post give that figure.

### Does Amazon Relay accept a Florida workers' comp exemption?
Amazon doesn't publish whether it accepts any state exemption. Florida says exemptions are issued to corporate officers and LLC members, not to the business, so ask Amazon what it accepts.

### Is workers' comp required in Texas?
The Texas Department of Insurance says private employers can choose to carry it and that it is not required in most cases. Amazon doesn't say how it treats Texas companies that don't carry it.

### Can occupational accident insurance replace workers' comp for Relay?
Amazon doesn't say. Its pages name workers' compensation and employer's liability only, so ask Amazon before you buy a substitute.

### Is there a phone number to ask Amazon Relay about insurance?
No. Amazon's FAQ says Relay doesn't have an official contact phone number. It points applicants to Contact Us on the top right of the application page.

# Does Amazon Relay pay a fuel surcharge?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-fuel-surcharge/
Published: 2026-10-23. Last updated: 2026-10-23.

Short answer: Yes. On spot loads it's inside the all-in price on the load board, with the base rate and tolls, not paid on top. In auctions you bid the base rate; fuel and tolls are paid after the load.

## Does Amazon Relay pay a fuel surcharge?

Yes, inside the price. Amazon's [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) says spot loads are booked at the all-in price, and "The base rate, fuel surcharges, and tolls charges are included."

So the number you see on the board already has fuel in it. Fuel isn't added on top of that price.

## How does the fuel surcharge show up on a load?

As one line of the payment breakdown on the load card. Amazon's [rates guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) (January 2026) splits the price into three parts:

| Part | What Amazon says |
|---|---|
| Base rate | "This is your payment for hauling the load, not including fuel or tolls." |
| Fuel surcharge | "It adjusts based on current fuel prices and is added in accordance with Relay Program Policies." |
| Tolls | Included in your total payout when the route uses toll roads |

Amazon's older [trucking work post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/booking-options/what-trucking-work-is-on-amazon-relay) put it this way: "We calculate fuel surcharge to carriers so that you're paid for fuel expenses as the market fluctuates."

## How is fuel handled in Relay auctions?

Differently. In an auction you bid only the base rate.

Amazon's [auctions guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/freight-bidding-on-amazon-relays-auctions) says accessorials, which it defines as fuel and tolls, are paid after the load is complete, and you don't include them in your bids. Leave fuel out of your number, or you'll bid against yourself. More in our [auctions guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auctions/).

## How does Amazon calculate the fuel surcharge?

It doesn't say in public. Amazon says the surcharge is added in accordance with the Relay Program Policies, which are behind the login, and no public page gives the formula or fuel index.

What you can see is the result: the fuel line in each load's payment breakdown. If a paid amount doesn't match it, our [payments guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-payments/) covers the 30-day payment dispute.

## How do you judge a Relay load after fuel?

Compare the all-in price with your full cost per mile. Amazon tells carriers to account for all-in business costs such as fuel, maintenance and insurance.

The common mistake is counting fuel twice. If you add the surcharge back on top of the posted price, or compare the all-in price with a base rate from another board, the load looks better than it is.

A quick check:

1. **Total miles.** Loaded miles plus deadhead to the pickup.
2. **Fuel cost.** Total miles divided by your MPG, times your diesel price.
3. **What's left.** The all-in price minus fuel, driver pay and your other costs.

Our free [Relay load calculator](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-load-calculator/) does this for you from the pay, loaded and deadhead miles, fuel price, MPG and other costs. For the bigger picture on rates, see [how much Amazon Relay pays](https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/) and [why Amazon Relay rates look so low](https://nudoiq.com/why-are-amazon-relay-rates-so-low/).

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ puts that math on the board. It's a Chrome extension for the Relay load board, independent and not affiliated with Amazon.

You enter your MPG, diesel price, driver pay and maintenance once in settings. Then every load card shows a net profit badge next to the price, so you see what's left after fuel without adding the surcharge twice.

AutoBook can book loads that clear your minimum net profit, up to a Max books number you set. Only auto-book loads you can run; cancels hurt your score.

Start your free week: 7 days free, no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month. Cancel anytime.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the fuel surcharge included in Amazon Relay rates?
Yes. Amazon says spot loads are booked at an all-in price that includes the base rate, fuel surcharge and tolls.

### Do I include fuel in an Amazon Relay auction bid?
No. Amazon says fuel and tolls are paid after the load is complete and aren't included in your bid. You bid the base rate.

### Does the Amazon Relay fuel surcharge change with diesel prices?
Amazon says it adjusts based on current fuel prices. It doesn't publish the index, the base price or the table it uses.

### Does Amazon Relay pay tolls?
Yes. Amazon says that if your route uses toll roads, the toll charge is included in your total payout.

### Where can I see the fuel surcharge on a Relay load?
In the payment breakdown on the load card. Amazon's rates guide says you see the payout upfront, split into base rate, fuel surcharge and tolls.

# Does Amazon Relay pay TONU when Amazon cancels your load?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-tonu/
Published: 2026-10-23. Last updated: 2026-10-23.

Short answer: Amazon publishes no TONU (truck ordered not used) policy for Relay. It says an Amazon cancellation won't hurt your score, the board suggests replacement loads, and blocks are typically paid in full. Pay disputes go through the Relay portal.

## Does Amazon Relay have a TONU policy?

Not one it publishes. TONU stands for truck ordered not used.

On October 14, 2026, we checked all 139 pages in relay.amazon.com's public sitemap. None gives a TONU amount or rule. Amazon's Relay Program Policies sit behind the login, so we can't see whether they cover it. Our [payments guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-payments/) found the same for detention and layover.

## Where do the TONU numbers online come from?

From Amazon Freight, not Relay. Amazon Freight's shipper terms list accessorial charges that Amazon Freight bills to shippers. Those aren't what Relay pays carriers, so don't plan around them.

## Does an Amazon cancellation hurt your score?

No. Amazon's [performance score page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-performance-score) says: "if we cancel tendered loads, their performance score won't be impacted."

Your own rejections are different. They count against acceptance, and the closer to pickup, the bigger the penalty. See [what happens if you cancel a load](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cancel-load/).

## What does Amazon offer when it cancels?

From Amazon's [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) and app page:

- **Replacement loads.** "Relay's load board suggests replacements for cancelled loads." Amazon adds: "We factor in the time and route constraints of the original load."
- **Driver alerts.** The [Relay app](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-truckers-use-the-amazon-relay-mobile-app) gives drivers "Cancellation alerts within 5 hours before the scheduled time."
- **Blocks.** "Blocks are typically paid in full even if your drivers and equipment aren't needed."

Amazon's [Post A Truck guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck) says the same for matched blocks: paid in full even if Amazon doesn't use the whole block. More on blocks in our [contracts guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contracts/).

## Why does Amazon Relay cancel loads?

One reason Amazon names in public is extreme weather. Its [2026 safety post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-safety/amazon-relays-2026-safety-innovations-whats-next) says that when its system can't find a route around extreme weather, "it automatically cancels the load" before the driver is on the road.

Amazon says: "About 200,000 loads have been cancelled by this technology, and replanned." The post doesn't say whether those loads were paid.

Carriers also report slow or missing pay on loads Amazon cancelled or cut mid-trip. That's what carriers say, not Amazon policy.

## What should you do when Amazon cancels your load?

1. **Screenshot the load card** and its payout before pickup.
2. **Write down the cancel time** and how you were told.
3. **Contact the ROC.** The Relay Operations Center runs 24/7, through the Relay portal or the Relay app.
4. **Check your weekly invoice.** Pay runs Sunday to Saturday and lands the following Friday.
5. **Dispute within 30 days.** Amazon's [FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says: "You can submit payment disputes directly through Amazon Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice."

Amazon doesn't say whether a cancelled load is paid, or whether the dispute route covers it. File anyway if the invoice looks wrong. Our [disputes guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-disputes/) covers each dispute type.

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ can't make Amazon pay a TONU. It's a Chrome extension for the Relay load board, independent and not affiliated with Amazon.

What it does help with is your record. During the free week and on the paid plan, its Pro View shows every stop's facility address and times right on the load card, so the details are on screen to screenshot before pickup. Each load also shows its net profit from costs you enter once.

If you use AutoBook, only auto-book loads you can run; cancels hurt your score. Start your free week: 7 days free, no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month. Cancel anytime.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Amazon Relay pay TONU?
Amazon doesn't publish a TONU policy or amount for Relay. If pay on a cancelled load looks wrong, file a payment dispute in the Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing your weekly invoice.

### Does an Amazon-cancelled load hurt my Relay score?
No. Amazon says loads it cancels won't affect your performance score. Loads you reject do count against acceptance.

### Are Relay blocks paid if Amazon doesn't use them?
Amazon says blocks are typically paid in full even if your drivers and equipment aren't needed.

### Why did Amazon Relay cancel my load?
We found no public list of cancel reasons. One Amazon names is extreme weather, when its system can't find a route around it.

### Who do I contact when Amazon cancels a load?
The Relay Operations Center (ROC), 24/7, through the Relay portal or the Relay app. Amazon says Relay has no official contact phone number.

# How do you add a driver on Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/how-to-add-a-driver-on-amazon-relay/
Published: 2026-10-23. Last updated: 2026-10-23.

Short answer: You invite the driver. Amazon says drivers can only create Relay profiles through invitations from Relay-approved carriers. The driver signs in to the Relay app with an Amazon account, enters CDL and contact details, and must pass the identity check.

## How do drivers get on your Relay account?

By invite only. After approval, Amazon's [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says: "Add your drivers and equipment to your Relay profile." It also says: "A carrier needs to invite their drivers to create a profile in the Relay app."

Amazon's [driver eligibility post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/driver-eligibility-requirements-to-haul-amazon-loads) is just as clear: "Drivers can only create Relay profiles through invitations from Relay-approved carriers."

Amazon's public pages don't show the click-by-click steps for sending an invite. What they do show is what happens after it.

## What does the driver do after the invite?

1. **Open the Relay app.** Log in to an existing Amazon account or create a new one.
2. **Enter the details.** CDL and contact information.
3. **Take the photos.** The license front and back, plus a selfie.
4. **Pass the checks.** "Only drivers who successfully complete an identification check can haul Relay loads."

Amazon typically reviews the information within 48 hours. Each driver needs their own login: "Drivers can't share their accounts." What each check looks at is in our [background check guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-background-check/), and the driver's side is in [Amazon Relay for drivers](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-drivers/).

## What are you responsible for as the carrier?

More than the invite. Amazon says "Carriers are responsible for their own drivers," which covers screening, hours of service, medical certification and license checks.

Two more lines from Amazon to keep in mind:

- "Carriers should only assign Amazon loads to drivers who have successfully passed background checks."
- "Multiple failed selfie checks can impact a driver's and carrier's access to Relay."

So don't promise a driver a load until they've cleared.

## How do you assign a Relay load to a driver?

You or your dispatcher book the load on the carrier's account, then put it on an invited driver who passed the checks. The driver runs it in the Relay app.

Keep the app open with location on for the whole trip. App usage is one of the four metrics in your [performance score](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/), so one driver who closes the app can pull your grade down. Our [app guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-app/) covers the driver side.

## Can you add a dispatcher to Amazon Relay?

Amazon's own security advice suggests you can. Its [email scams post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/email-scams-how-to-spot-a-fake) tells carriers to check their "Admin/dispatcher list: Is everyone someone you approved?"

But Amazon doesn't publish the steps or the role names for adding a dispatcher user. The rules that do apply:

- A dispatcher works inside the carrier's own account.
- Never share or resell access to your account.
- No subcontracting or double brokering.

More on the job itself in our [dispatcher guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-dispatcher/).

## How do you keep strangers off your Relay account?

Log in and check it often. The same Amazon post lists what to look at:

| Check | What to ask |
|---|---|
| Driver list | "Do you recognize every driver?" |
| Admin/dispatcher list | Is everyone someone you approved? |
| Recent loads | Did your company book each one? |
| Bank details | Are they still yours? |

Amazon warns that scammers who get in "can access your account, add unauthorized drivers, and book loads they intend to steal." And: "Amazon Relay will never request Relay carrier's sensitive account information, password or the one-time password." See our [fraud guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-fraud/).

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

If you or a dispatcher watch the board for several trucks, NudoIQ works in your own Chrome, on the carrier's signed-in Relay tab. It never asks for the Amazon password. It's independent, not affiliated with Amazon.

- **Refresh** the board at a pace you set
- **Alert** with a sound when a matching load appears
- **Net profit** on each load, from costs you enter once
- **AutoBook** loads that clear your minimum net profit, up to a Max books number you set. Only auto-book loads you can run; cancels hurt your score.

Start your free week: 7 days free, no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month. Cancel anytime.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a driver sign up for Amazon Relay on their own?
No. Amazon says drivers can only create Relay profiles through invitations from Relay-approved carriers.

### How long does Amazon Relay driver verification take?
Amazon says it typically reviews the CDL and selfie within 48 hours. The driver can't haul Relay loads until the identity check is passed.

### Can two drivers share one Relay login?
No. Amazon says drivers can't share their accounts, so each driver needs their own profile.

### How do I add a dispatcher to my Amazon Relay account?
Amazon doesn't publish the steps or role names. Its security post tells carriers to review their admin/dispatcher list and make sure everyone on it is someone they approved.

### Will Amazon Relay ask for my password?
No. Amazon says Relay will never request a carrier's sensitive account information, password or one-time password.

# How do you get loads on Amazon Relay?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/how-to-get-loads-on-amazon-relay/
Published: 2026-10-23. Last updated: 2026-10-23.

Short answer: Get approved as a Relay carrier, add your drivers and equipment, then book spot loads on the Relay load board. You can also post your truck with Post A Truck, and book contracts and auctions once your grade allows.

## What do you need before you can get Relay loads?

An approved Relay carrier account. Amazon's [get started page](https://relay.amazon.com/get-started) asks for:

- Valid MC and DOT numbers with interstate authority
- DOT authority that has been active for 180 days or more
- The insurance and safety minimums listed on that page

You can still apply before your authority reaches 180 days. Amazon's [FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says an application is typically approved or rejected within 1 to 3 weeks. The full list is in our [Amazon Relay requirements guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

## What are the steps to get your first load?

Amazon's [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) gives the next steps after approval:

1. **Add your drivers and equipment.** Amazon says: "Add your drivers and equipment to your Relay profile." See [how to add a driver](https://nudoiq.com/how-to-add-a-driver-on-amazon-relay/).
2. **Search the load board.** Amazon says searches "begin with your starting point and destination."
3. **Filter.** Trailer status, equipment type, load type, driver type, max stops and trip length.
4. **Open the load card.** It shows the stops, times, payment breakdown and requirements.
5. **Book it.** In Amazon's words: "Start booking loads directly through the Relay load board."

Amazon's [free freight search post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-to-find-truck-loads-faster-with-amazon-relays-free-freight-search) says approved carriers get 24/7 access, and its [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) says you can "search and book without any fees."

## What else on the board helps you find loads?

From Amazon's load board guide:

- **Saved searches.** "Save your company's most used searches."
- **Alerts.** "Opt in to email alerts for real-time updates on new spot loads." The Relay app sends push notifications too.
- **Auto-refresh.** Amazon says its board refreshes new spot matches on its own.
- **Pickup time.** On some loads you can choose a better pickup time from a list.
- **Name your price.** "On select spot loads, you have the opportunity to name your own price." Relay Assistant reviews your number.
- **Return trips.** The board recommends loads for the way back.

Amazon's [free freight search post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-to-find-truck-loads-faster-with-amazon-relays-free-freight-search) adds load picks based on your search history. More in our [load board guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/).

## What are the other ways to get Relay loads?

| Way in | How it works | Grade needed |
|---|---|---|
| Post A Truck | Post when and where your truck is free, with a minimum rate. Amazon books matching loads for you. | Higher grades matched first |
| Contracts | Weekly work at set pay | B or higher for new contracts |
| Auctions | You bid your own rate | C+ or higher (reefer: B) |

With [Post A Truck](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck), you set a radius, max deadhead, cities, one-way or round trip, and a minimum rate per mile or payout, up to 2 weeks out. Amazon says it "gives you first access advantage to all freight available during the time frame you set before it becomes available on the load board."

Blocks, time-based work, are another option. See our guides to [Post A Truck](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-post-a-truck/) and [contracts](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contracts/).

## Why do good Relay loads disappear so fast?

1. **Post A Truck books first.** It matches loads, often before they reach the board. Amazon's [grades guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) says: "If an A+ carrier and a B+ carrier both post for the same load, the A+ carrier gets matched first."
2. **Higher grades see loads first.** The same guide says A+, A and B+ carriers "get first pick of new spot loads and contracts."

So speed helps on the loads you can see. Your grade decides what you see. If your board looks thin, read [why the load board isn't showing loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board-not-showing-loads/) and our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/).

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that works on the Relay load board in your own signed-in tab. It's independent, not affiliated with Amazon. On the search you've already set, it can:

- **Refresh** the board at a pace you set
- **Alert** you with a sound when a matching load appears
- **Show net profit** on each load, from costs you enter once
- **AutoBook** loads that clear your minimum net profit, up to a Max books number you set. Only auto-book loads you can run; cancels hurt your score.
- **Instant Book** a load in one tap, with no confirmation screen

It can't show loads Amazon hasn't offered you. Start your free week: 7 days free, no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month. Cancel anytime. [See how NudoIQ works](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-chrome-extension/).

## Frequently asked questions

### How long does it take to get loads on Amazon Relay?
Amazon's FAQ says an application is typically approved or rejected within 1 to 3 weeks. After that, you add your drivers and equipment and start booking on the load board.

### Does it cost anything to book loads on Amazon Relay?
No. Amazon says you can search and book on the Relay load board without any fees.

### Can a new carrier get loads on Amazon Relay?
Yes, once approved. Amazon asks for DOT authority active 180 days or more, but says you can apply sooner. Contracts need a B grade or higher and auctions C+ or higher.

### Why can't I see good loads on Amazon Relay?
Some are booked through Post A Truck before they reach the board. A+, A and B+ carriers also see new spot loads first, so a higher grade can change what you see.

### Can I set my own rate on Amazon Relay?
In a few ways. Post A Truck takes a minimum rate per mile or payout, auctions take your bid, and on select spot loads you can name your own price.

# Why are Amazon Relay rates so low?

URL: https://nudoiq.com/why-are-amazon-relay-rates-so-low/
Published: 2026-10-23. Last updated: 2026-10-23.

Short answer: Relay rates move with demand, season and region, and the posted price is all-in (base, fuel, tolls), so it can look low next to a base rate elsewhere. Deadhead and your grade matter too: higher grades see new loads first.

## Why do Amazon Relay rates look so low?

Mostly because they move, and Amazon says so. From its [rates guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates):

- **Demand.** "Rates fluctuate. Demand shifts."
- **Season and region.** "Seasonal demand fluctuations and regional market conditions will still impact the rates."
- **Your search.** "being specific with your load search filters can influence the price you see."

Amazon adds: "Live rates are provided at the time of booking." So the price you see now can differ from the same lane an hour later.

## Are you comparing the right number?

Often not. The posted price on Relay is all-in: base rate, fuel surcharge and tolls together.

Compare it with your own all-in cost per mile. Don't compare it with a base rate on another board, and don't add fuel back on top. Our [fuel surcharge guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-fuel-surcharge/) explains the breakdown.

## How does deadhead make a rate worse?

Amazon's rates guide lists "Distance (including length of deadhead, roundtrip, one-way)" as a price factor.

The empty miles to the pickup and back home cost you fuel and time, but the load pays only what's posted. A rate that looks fine per loaded mile can fall below your cost once deadhead is counted. Run the numbers in our free [Relay load calculator](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-load-calculator/).

## Does your grade change what you see?

It changes access. Amazon's [grades guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) says A+, A and B+ carriers "get first pick of new spot loads and contracts."

Post A Truck also matches some loads before they reach the board, and higher grades are matched first. So a lower grade can mean a thinner, later board, with the better loads already gone. Amazon doesn't say a grade changes what a load pays. See our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/).

## What do carriers say about Relay rates?

This part is what carriers say, not Amazon policy:

- Rates feel "take it or leave it."
- Some carriers treat Relay as backhaul filler.
- Some carriers say it pays better in peak: around Prime Day and from October to December.

Our [peak season guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-peak-season/) covers those weeks.

## What can you do about low Relay rates?

Amazon gives you several ways to set your own number. Its [rates guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) names Post A Truck, auctions and Relay Assistant. Contracts come from its [grades guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) and name your price from its [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board):

| Lever | What you control |
|---|---|
| Post A Truck | "You specify your rate per mile, and loads come to you." |
| Auctions | "You offer the rate that works for your business, and if you win, that rate is locked in for the entire contract." |
| Contracts | Weekly work at set pay, grade B or higher |
| Relay Assistant | "Top-performing carriers can negotiate rates on urgent spot loads through AI-powered chat." |
| Name your price | Offered on select spot loads |

Two more things you control: know what a lane paid before, and skip loads that don't cover your cost. Our [Amazon Relay rates page](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-rates/) shows how posted prices moved while loads sat on the board. More on each lever in our guides to [Post A Truck](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-post-a-truck/) and [auctions](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auctions/).

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ can't raise a rate. It helps you judge one. It's a Chrome extension for the Relay load board, independent and not affiliated with Amazon.

- **Price History.** Button 1 under each load opens Lane Intelligence, so you can see what that lane paid before.
- **Net profit.** Each load shows its net from costs you enter once.
- **AutoBook.** Books loads only at or above your minimum net profit, up to a Max books number you set. Only auto-book loads you can run; cancels hurt your score.

Start your free week: 7 days free, no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month. Cancel anytime.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why are Amazon Relay rates so low right now?
Amazon says rates shift with demand, season and regional market conditions. Carriers say rates tend to be better in peak, around Prime Day and from October to December.

### Does Amazon Relay pay fuel on top of the rate?
No. Spot loads are priced all-in, with the base rate, fuel surcharge and tolls included in the posted price.

### Can you negotiate rates on Amazon Relay?
On some loads. Amazon says top-performing carriers can negotiate on urgent spot loads through Relay Assistant, and select spot loads let you name your own price. Amazon decides whether to accept.

### Do higher grades get better rates on Amazon Relay?
Amazon doesn't say a grade changes a load's price. Higher grades get first pick of new spot loads and contracts, and are matched first on Post A Truck.

### Is Amazon Relay worth it with these rates?
It depends on your own costs and lanes. Our guide on [whether Amazon Relay is worth it](https://nudoiq.com/is-amazon-relay-worth-it/) walks through how to decide.
